studies.title: Some is not enough: quantifier comprehension in corticobasal syndrome and behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia.
studies.abstract: Quantifiers are very common in everyday speech, but we know little about their cognitive basis or neural representation. The present study examined comprehension of three classes of quantifiers that depend on different cognitive components in patients with focal neurodegenerative diseases. Patients evaluated the truth-value of a sentence containing a quantifier relative to a picture illustrating a small number of familiar objects, and performance was related to MRI grey matter atrophy using voxel-based morphometry. We found that patients with corticobasal syndrome (CBS) and posterior cortical atrophy (PCA) are significantly impaired in their comprehension of cardinal quantifiers (e.g. "At least three birds are on the branch"), due in part to their deficit in quantity knowledge. MRI analyses related this deficit to temporal-parietal atrophy found in CBS/PCA. We also found that patients with behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) are significantly impaired in their comprehension of logical quantifiers (e.g. "Some of the birds are on the branch"), associated with a simple form of perceptual logic, and this correlated with their deficit on executive measures. This deficit was related to disease in rostral prefrontal cortex in bvFTD. These patients were also impaired in their comprehension of majority quantifiers (e.g. "At least half of the birds are on the branch"), and this too was correlated with their deficit on executive measures. This was related to disease in the basal ganglia interrupting a frontal-striatal loop critical for executive functioning. These findings suggest that a large-scale frontal-parietal neural network plays a crucial role in quantifier comprehension, and that comprehension of specific classes of quantifiers may be selectively impaired in patients with focal neurodegenerative conditions in these areas.

studies.title: Dissociation of quantifiers and object nouns in speech in focal neurodegenerative disease.
studies.abstract: Quantifiers such as many and some are thought to depend in part on the conceptual representation of number knowledge, while object nouns such as cookie and boy appear to depend in part on visual feature knowledge associated with object concepts. Further, number knowledge is associated with a frontal-parietal network while object knowledge is related in part to anterior and ventral portions of the temporal lobe. We examined the cognitive and anatomic basis for the spontaneous speech production of quantifiers and object nouns in non-aphasic patients with focal neurodegenerative disease associated with corticobasal syndrome (CBS, n=33), behavioral variant frontotemporal degeneration (bvFTD, n=54), and semantic variant primary progressive aphasia (svPPA, n=19). We recorded a semi-structured speech sample elicited from patients and healthy seniors (n=27) during description of the Cookie Theft scene. We observed a dissociation: CBS and bvFTD were significantly impaired in the production of quantifiers but not object nouns, while svPPA were significantly impaired in the production of object nouns but not quantifiers. MRI analysis revealed that quantifier production deficits in CBS and bvFTD were associated with disease in a frontal-parietal network important for number knowledge, while impaired production of object nouns in all patient groups was related to disease in inferior temporal regions important for representations of visual feature knowledge of objects. These findings imply that partially dissociable representations in semantic memory may underlie different segments of the lexicon.

studies.title: Getting on the same page: the neural basis for social coordination deficits in behavioral variant frontotemporal degeneration.
studies.abstract: For social interactions to be successful, individuals must establish shared mental representations that allow them to reach a common understanding and "get on the same page". We refer to this process as social coordination. While examples of social coordination are ubiquitous in daily life, relatively little is known about the neuroanatomic basis of this complex behavior. This is particularly true in a language context, as previous studies have used overly complex paradigms to study this. Although traditional views of language processing and the recent interactive-alignment account of conversation focus on peri-Sylvian regions, our model of social coordination predicts prefrontal involvement. To test this hypothesis, we examine the neural basis of social coordination during conversational exchanges in non-aphasic patients with behavioral variant frontotemporal degeneration (bvFTD). bvFTD patients show impairments in executive function and social comportment due to disease in frontal and anterior temporal regions. To investigate social coordination in bvFTD, we developed a novel language-based task that assesses patients' ability to convey an object's description to a conversational partner. Experimental conditions manipulated the amount of information shared by the participant and the conversational partner, and the associated working memory demands. Our results indicate that, although patients did not have difficulty identifying the features of the objects, they did produce descriptions that included insufficient or inappropriate adjectives and thus struggled to communicate effectively. Impaired performance was related to gray matter atrophy particularly in medial prefrontal and orbitofrontal cortices. Our findings suggest an important role for non-language brain areas that belong to a large-scale neurocognitive network for social coordination.

studies.title: Glucose metabolism and serotonin receptors in the frontotemporal lobe degeneration.
studies.abstract: In patients with the frontal variant of frontotemporal lobar degeneration (fv-FTLD), behavioral abnormalities may vary from apathy with motor slowness (apathetic form) to disinhibition with agitation (disinhibited form). These clinical presentations may be related to specific regional cerebral dysfunction and to deficit in the serotoninergic system. We studied cerebral glucose uptake using (18)F-fluorodeoxyglucose and positron emission tomography in 18 patients fulfilling clinical criteria for fv-FTLD and showing, respectively, an apathetic or disinhibited behavioral syndrome. In eight of these patients, we also evaluated the 5-hydroxytryptamine-2A receptor cerebral receptor distribution with [(11)C]MDL and positron emission tomography. We found a reduction of frontal glucose metabolism in the whole group of fv-FTLD patients. Apathetic syndrome was associated with a prevalent dorsolateral and frontal medial hypometabolism, whereas the disinhibited syndrome demonstrated a selective hypometabolism in interconnected limbic structures (the cingulate cortex, hippocampus/amygdala, and accumbens nucleus). The in vivo measurements of [(11)C]MDL indicated a significant reduction of 5-hydroxytryptamine-2A receptors in orbitofrontal, frontal medial, and cingulate cortices. These (18)F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography changes can be considered as specific functional markers of the different behavioral presentations in fv-FTLD. The serotoninergic system dysfunction provides a rationale for therapeutic trials with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors.

studies.abstract: In a multicenter study, FDG-PET images in a population of 29 patients with frontotemporal dementia (FTD) were compared to controls with similar age from each center. A conjunction analysis led to identification of the ventromedial frontopolar cortex as the single region affected in each and every FTD patients. This precise regional metabolic impairment should be integrated with recent neuropsychological researches, such as those showing that the ventromedial frontal cortex is critically involved in decision-making processes based on personal experience, feelings of rightness or social knowledge, processes that are characteristically impaired in FTD.

studies.title: The Effect of Gray Matter ICA and Coefficient of Variation Mapping of BOLD Data on the Detection of Functional Connectivity Changes in Alzheimer's Disease and bvFTD.
studies.abstract: Resting-state fMRI results in neurodegenerative diseases have been somewhat conflicting. This may be due to complex partial volume effects of CSF in BOLD signal in patients with brain atrophy. To encounter this problem, we used a coefficient of variation (CV) map to highlight artifacts in the data, followed by analysis of gray matter voxels in order to minimize brain volume effects between groups. The effects of these measures were compared to whole brain ICA dual regression results in Alzheimer's disease (AD) and behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD). 23 AD patients, 21 bvFTD patients and 25 healthy controls were included. The quality of the data was controlled by CV mapping. For detecting functional connectivity (FC) differences whole brain ICA (wbICA) and also segmented gray matter ICA (gmICA) followed by dual regression were conducted, both of which were performed both before and after data quality control. Decreased FC was detected in posterior DMN in the AD group and in the Salience network in the bvFTD group after combining CV quality control with gmICA. Before CV quality control, the decreased connectivity finding was not detectable in gmICA in neither of the groups. Same finding recurred when exclusion was based on randomization. The subjects excluded due to artifacts noticed in the CV maps had significantly lower temporal signal-to-noise ratio than the included subjects. Data quality measure CV is an effective tool in detecting artifacts from resting state analysis. CV reflects temporal dispersion of the BOLD signal stability and may thus be most helpful for spatial ICA, which has a blind spot in spatially correlating widespread artifacts. CV mapping in conjunction with gmICA yields results suiting previous findings both in AD and bvFTD.

studies.title: GroupICA dual regression analysis of resting state networks in a behavioral variant of frontotemporal dementia.
studies.abstract: Functional MRI studies have revealed changes in default-mode and salience networks in neurodegenerative dementias, especially in Alzheimer's disease (AD). The purpose of this study was to analyze the whole brain cortex resting state networks (RSNs) in patients with behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) by using resting state functional MRI (rfMRI). The group specific RSNs were identified by high model order independent component analysis (ICA) and a dual regression technique was used to detect between-group differences in the RSNs with p < 0.05 threshold corrected for multiple comparisons. A y-concatenation method was used to correct for multiple comparisons for multiple independent components, gray matter differences as well as the voxel level. We found increased connectivity in several networks within patients with bvFTD compared to the control group. The most prominent enhancement was seen in the right frontotemporal area and insula. A significant increase in functional connectivity was also detected in the left dorsal attention network (DAN), in anterior paracingulate-a default mode sub-network as well as in the anterior parts of the frontal pole. Notably the increased patterns of connectivity were seen in areas around atrophic regions. The present results demonstrate abnormal increased connectivity in several important brain networks including the DAN and default-mode network (DMN) in patients with bvFTD. These changes may be associated with decline in executive functions and attention as well as apathy, which are the major cognitive and neuropsychiatric defects in patients with frontotemporal dementia.

studies.title: Your perspective and my benefit: multiple lesion models of self-other integration strategies during social bargaining.
studies.abstract: Recursive social decision-making requires the use of flexible, context-sensitive long-term strategies for negotiation. To succeed in social bargaining, participants' own perspectives must be dynamically integrated with those of interactors to maximize self-benefits and adapt to the other's preferences, respectively. This is a prerequisite to develop a successful long-term self-other integration strategy. While such form of strategic interaction is critical to social decision-making, little is known about its neurocognitive correlates. To bridge this gap, we analysed social bargaining behaviour in relation to its structural neural correlates, ongoing brain dynamics (oscillations and related source space), and functional connectivity signatures in healthy subjects and patients offering contrastive lesion models of neurodegeneration and focal stroke: behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia, Alzheimer's disease, and frontal lesions. All groups showed preserved basic bargaining indexes. However, impaired self-other integration strategy was found in patients with behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia and frontal lesions, suggesting that social bargaining critically depends on the integrity of prefrontal regions. Also, associations between behavioural performance and data from voxel-based morphometry and voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping revealed a critical role of prefrontal regions in value integration and strategic decisions for self-other integration strategy. Furthermore, as shown by measures of brain dynamics and related sources during the task, the self-other integration strategy was predicted by brain anticipatory activity (alpha/beta oscillations with sources in frontotemporal regions) associated with expectations about others' decisions. This pattern was reduced in all clinical groups, with greater impairments in behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia and frontal lesions than Alzheimer's disease. Finally, connectivity analysis from functional magnetic resonance imaging evidenced a fronto-temporo-parietal network involved in successful self-other integration strategy, with selective compromise of long-distance connections in frontal disorders. In sum, this work provides unprecedented evidence of convergent behavioural and neurocognitive signatures of strategic social bargaining in different lesion models. Our findings offer new insights into the critical roles of prefrontal hubs and associated temporo-parietal networks for strategic social negotiation.

studies.title: Structural Anatomical Investigation of Long-Term Memory Deficit in Behavioral Frontotemporal Dementia.
studies.abstract: Although a growing body of work has shown that behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) could present with severe amnesia in approximately half of cases, memory assessment is currently the clinical standard to distinguish bvFTD from Alzheimer's disease (AD). Thus, the concept of "relatively preserved episodic memory" in bvFTD remains the basis of its clinical distinction from AD and a criterion for bvFTD's diagnosis. This view is supported by the idea that bvFTD is not characterized by genuine amnesia and hippocampal degeneration, by contrast to AD. In this multicenter study, we aimed to investigate the neural correlates of memory performance in bvFTD as assessed by the Free and Cued Selective Reminding Test (FCSRT). Imaging explorations followed a two-step procedure, first relying on a visual rating of atrophy of 35 bvFTD and 34 AD patients' MRI, contrasted with 29 controls; and then using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) in a subset of bvFTD patients. Results showed that 43% of bvFTD patients presented with a genuine amnesia. Data-driven analysis on visual rating data showed that, in bvFTD, memory recall & storage performances were significantly predicted by atrophy in rostral prefrontal and hippocampal/perihippocampal regions, similar to mild AD. VBM results in bvFTD (pFWE<0.05) showed similar prefrontal and hippocampal regions in addition to striatal and lateral temporal involvement. Our findings showed the involvement of prefrontal as well as medial/lateral temporal atrophy in memory deficits of bvFTD patients. This contradicts the common view that only frontal deficits explain memory impairment in this disease and plead for an updated view on memory dysfunctions in bvFTD.

studies.title: Frontotemporal dementia as a neural system disease.
studies.abstract: Some brain structures atrophic in frontotemporal dementia (FTD) belong to the rostral limbic system (RLS), that regulates context-dependent behaviors after evaluation of the motivational content of stimuli. The clinical manifestations of FTD are consistent with its impairment. Aim of this study was to assess whole brain morphology in FTD using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and voxel-based morphometry with statistic parametric mapping (SPM99) to test the hypothesis that the RLS might be specifically targeted by FTD. Nine FTD patients and 26 healthy controls underwent high resolution 3D MRI. SPM99 performed (a) spatial normalization to a customized template, (b) segmentation, (c) smoothing, (d) voxel-by-voxel comparison of gray matter between cases and controls. P was set at 0.05 corrected for multiple comparisons. All but one regions of the RLS (the periaqueductal gray) were atrophic in FTD. At P<0.001 uncorrected also the periaqueductal gray was atrophic. Atrophy outside the RLS was confined to a few voxels in the frontal and temporal gyri. FTD might be a neural-system disease where the RLS is predominantly damaged.

studies.title: Executive and behavioral deficits share common neural substrates in frontotemporal lobar degeneration - a pilot FDG-PET study.
studies.abstract: Behavioral and executive dysfunctions are typical symptoms of frontotemporal lobar degeneration, associated with its subtypes frontotemporal and semantic dementia. Although both functions depend on the frontal lobes, no study has yet compared their neural correlates in frontotemporal lobar degeneration. Accordingly, we correlated clinical scores of behavioral and executive deficits with glucose utilization as measured by [(18)F]fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography in 17 patients with frontotemporal lobar degeneration and 9 age- and sex-matched control subjects. Impairment in executive functions was measured by the Behavioral Assessment of the Dysexecutive Syndrome, a modified Stroop paradigm and/or the Tower of Toronto Test. Behavioral deficits were examined with the Neuropsychiatric Inventory. Executive dysfunction was correlated with diminished glucose utilization in frontomedial and frontolateral cortices. Brain regions included the anterior cingulate and midcingulate gyri, anterior medial frontal cortex, and left frontolateral cortex. Behavioral deficits were associated with mainly frontomedial networks, particularly the anterior medial frontal cortex, gyrus rectus, and area subcallosa. Our pilot study reveals partially overlapping neural correlates of executive and behavioral dysfunction in frontotemporal lobar degeneration. The results suggest that some behavioral deficits, namely disinhibition and appetite and eating abnormalities, are particularly related to executive dysfunction. This hypothesis might be further explored in studies involving larger patient groups.

studies.title: Neuroanatomical correlates of apathy and disinhibition in behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia.
studies.abstract: Neuroanatomical correlates of apathy and disinhibition, behavioral abnormalities in behavioral variant Frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) remain unclear. In this study 45 participants (25 bvFTD patients and 20 controls) provided data on clinical, neuropsychological, behavioral (on Frontal Systems Behavior (FrSBe) Scale), cortical volume (on voxel-based morphometry (VBM)) and tract based spatial fractional anisotropy ((FA) on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), allowing examination of the neural correlates of apathy and disinhibition. The patients with bvFTD had predominant grey matter loss and corresponding white matter fractional anisotropy reduction in the frontal and temporal lobe compared to the controls. Grey matter loss in frontal, temporal and limbic structures correlated with apathy and degeneration in temporal limbic brain areas correlated with disinhibition. FA changes in inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus and forceps minor correlated with apathy and fibre integrity changes in the superior longitudinal fasciculus correlated with disinhibition. The current study suggests that apathy and disinhibition arises due to changes in the frontal, temporal and limbic brain areas  in bvFTD.

studies.title: Understanding social dysfunction in the behavioural variant of frontotemporal dementia: the role of emotion and sarcasm processing.
studies.abstract: Social interaction is profoundly affected in the behavioural form of frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) yet there are few means of objectively assessing this. Diagnosis of bvFTD is based on informant report, however a number of individuals with a clinical profile consistent with the disease have no imaging abnormality and seem to remain stable, with doubt about the presence of underlying neurodegenerative pathology. We aimed to quantify aspects of the behavioural disorder and link it to the underlying level of atrophy in socially relevant brain regions. We tested individuals with either bvFTD (N = 26) or Alzheimer's disease (N = 9) and 16 controls using The Awareness of Social Inference Test (TASIT) to assess their ability to identify emotion and sarcasm in video vignettes. A subset of bvFTD patients (N = 21) and controls (N = 12) were scanned using MRI within 6 months of assessment. There was marked impairment in the ability of bvFTD patients whose scans showed abnormalities to recognize sarcastic, but not sincere statements. Their capacity to interpret negative emotion was also impaired, and this appeared to be a major factor underlying the deficit in sarcasm recognition. Clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients whose scans were normal, Alzheimer's disease patients and controls had no difficulty in appreciating both types of statement. In a multivariate imaging analysis it was shown that the sarcasm (and emotion recognition) deficit was dependent on a circuit involving the lateral orbitofrontal cortex, insula, amygdala and temporal pole, particularly on the right. Performance on a more global test of cognitive function, the Addenbrooke's Cognitive Examination did not have a unique association with these regions. The TASIT is an objective test of social dysfunction in bvFTD which indexes the frontotemporal volume loss in bvFTD patients and provides an objective measure for separating behavioural patients who are likely to decline from those who may remain stable. These results provide additional evidence for the role of the orbitofrontal cortex and related structures in the processing of socially relevant signals, particularly those where negative emotion recognition is important.

studies.title: Functional MRI of music emotion processing in frontotemporal dementia.
studies.abstract: Frontotemporal dementia is an important neurodegenerative disorder of younger life led by profound emotional and social dysfunction. Here we used fMRI to assess brain mechanisms of music emotion processing in a cohort of patients with frontotemporal dementia (n = 15) in relation to healthy age-matched individuals (n = 11). In a passive-listening paradigm, we manipulated levels of emotion processing in simple arpeggio chords (mode versus dissonance) and emotion modality (music versus human emotional vocalizations). A complex profile of disease-associated functional alterations was identified with separable signatures of musical mode, emotion level, and emotion modality within a common, distributed brain network, including posterior and anterior superior temporal and inferior frontal cortices and dorsal brainstem effector nuclei. Separable functional signatures were identified post-hoc in patients with and without abnormal craving for music (musicophilia): a model for specific abnormal emotional behaviors in frontotemporal dementia. Our findings indicate the potential of music to delineate neural mechanisms of altered emotion processing in dementias, with implications for future disease tracking and therapeutic strategies.

fulltext_screening_results.reason: Although this study includes VBM analyses (I3), clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (I4) with adequate group size (n=48; I5), and reports group-level whole-brain VBM results (I7) described in text/figures (I8), it does not present a whole-brain between-group imaging contrast that directly compares the bvFTD group to healthy controls. The reported VBM contrasts are primarily AD versus bvFTD (patient vs patient), and the imaging cohort lacks a concurrent healthy control imaging comparison for bvFTD. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (bvFTD vs controls imaging contrast in MNI/Talairach space) is not met, so the study must be excluded.

The study uses whole-brain VBM (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=16) (I4), and has sufficient sample sizes for patient and control groups (I5). However, it does not report any between-group voxelwise contrast (bvFTD vs. healthy controls) in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) specific to the bvFTD group. The VBM analyses reported are brain–behavior correlations across the entire mixed diagnostic sample and co-atrophy-adjusted maps, not group-level bvFTD vs. control contrasts; no bvFTD-specific whole-brain voxelwise results are presented in the main text (I6 and I7 not met). Therefore it fails the requirement for a group-level between-group whole-brain result for the target sample. No exclusion criteria from the list are met. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion criteria met: E6. This study used VBM (I3 satisfied) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4 satisfied) with sufficient sample sizes (bvFTD n=13; controls n=20; I5 satisfied). However, the VBM analyses reported in the paper are correlations within the combined patient cohort and significant findings are reported only within pre-specified regional volumes of interest (ROI-level, FWE-corrected within ROIs). The paper does not report any between-group voxelwise contrast in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing the bvFTD group alone versus controls, nor any whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results attributable to the bvFTD group (I6 and I7 not met). Therefore it meets exclusion E6 (only ROI results/no qualifying whole-brain between-group voxelwise result). Full text appears complete and sufficient for assessment (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it performed a voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analysis (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=22) according to consensus criteria (I4) with adequate sample sizes for patient and control groups (bvFTD n=22; controls n=34) meeting the >=6 requirement (I5). The VBM was conducted in standard space (registration to MNI template) and patient-control voxelwise comparisons were reported (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results with TFCE and permutation testing), with bvFTD vs. controls contrasts described and results provided in supplementary figures (I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (no review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, empirical data, not limited to excluded modalities). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and acknowledgements present).

Exclusion reason: E6 applies — the study reports ROI-based structural MRI volume analyses (summed frontotemporal atlas regions) and does not report whole-brain, voxelwise results in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). Inclusion met: I5 (patient and control groups both >6 participants: 105 carriers, 69 noncarriers). Inclusions not met: I3 (imaging modality is not VBM, task/resting‑state fMRI, or FDG‑PET as required), I4 (sample is autosomal dominant FTLD mutation carriers, not a clinically-diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s disease group as specified), I6 (no between-group contrast reported in stereotactic coordinates comparing a bvFTD group to controls), and I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper is excluded.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses resting-state fMRI (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group (n=21) and matched controls (I4, I5), and reports voxelwise between-group contrasts (two-sample t tests) comparing bvFTD to controls assessed in standard space (MNI coordinates used for seeds and voxelwise analyses) with whole-brain, cluster-level corrected results (satisfying I6 and I7). Results are presented in figures and described in text (acceptable per I8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the article appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (no review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, no disallowed comorbid sample, empirical original data, and not limited solely to excluded modalities). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the review.

The study uses VBM and includes adequate sample sizes, but it does not specifically investigate or report results for behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) as a distinct group. The FTD sample is heterogeneous (15 PPA variants; 14 with social/executive dysfunction) and all analyses are reported for the pooled FTD group versus controls; no bvFTD-only between-group voxelwise contrasts or coordinates are provided. Therefore it fails the requirement for inclusion of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients analyzed separately and fails the requirement for bvFTD-specific between-group whole-brain contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I5 (sample sizes ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (bvFTD-specific sample), I6 (bvFTD vs control contrast not reported), I7 (bvFTD-specific whole-brain result not provided). No exclusion criteria from the list (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study uses T1-weighted volumetric segmentation of amygdala subnuclei (ROI-based structural volumetry), not one of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), and it does not report whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results or stereotactic coordinates. Therefore exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) applies. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes Pick's disease patients among pathological groups) and I5 (patient and control groups both exceed 6 participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach stereotactic space comparing bvFTD to controls), and I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD/FTLD patients (I4), has sufficient sample sizes (7 FTLD with stereotypies, 10 FTLD without, and matched controls) meeting the >=6 requirement (I5), reports voxelwise between-group contrasts in MNI stereotactic space comparing the bvFTD/FTLD groups to controls (I6) using whole-brain VBM analyses (I7), and the whole-brain results are described in the text/figures (I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not a review, not ROI-only, no disallowed modalities or comorbid-sample issues). Note: sample is modest and some secondary analyses used uncorrected thresholds, but these caveats do not violate inclusion/exclusion rules.

This study meets inclusion criteria I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes a clinically diagnosed bv-FTD group of n=15), and I5 (bvFTD n=15 and controls n=15). However, it does NOT report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrast directly comparing the bvFTD group to controls in a standardized stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The reported VBM analyses are (a) a comparison of a mixed ‘poor melody score’ patient subgroup (patients with mixed diagnoses) vs controls and (b) covariate/correlation analyses across all patients merged together. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not satisfied (no bvFTD vs control voxelwise contrast reported), so the study cannot be included for the meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria from the provided list are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: it does not report a between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space. The paper reports within-group VBM regression analyses correlating reward-seeking scores in a bvFTD-only sample (group-level voxelwise results), not a bvFTD vs control whole-brain comparison. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses voxel-based morphometry), I4 (sample comprises clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD patients), I5 (patient sample n=91 for imaging analyses, ≥6), I7 (reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results from the target bvFTD sample), I8 (results reported in MNI coordinates). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review. It used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality (I3). The sample includes a clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bv-FTD) subgroup (n=27) (I4) and a healthy control group (n=14), satisfying the minimum group sizes (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses with results in MNI space (coordinates provided for significant clusters) and describes between-group VBM comparisons (each diagnostic group vs controls) referenced in the text and supplementary table (fulfilling I6, I7). Reporting of voxelwise results in the main text and supplementary materials meets the allowance for coordinates/figures/supplements (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: this is an empirical VBM study (not a review), it reports whole-brain results (not ROI-only), and does not rely on excluded modalities. Therefore I include the study.

This is an original empirical study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry and resting-state fMRI (seed-based analyses). The sample includes 87 bvFTD patients (21 with criminal behavior) and 26 healthy controls, meeting sample-size requirements. The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-/vertex-wise results (with MNI normalization and x,y,z coordinates) comparing bvFTD subgroups and bvFTD vs. controls, and provides region-based analyses and figures/tables. Full methods, results, and discussion are present; supplemental material is not required for core outcomes. Although a small subset of patients had histories of alcohol/drug abuse (4/21), the primary sample and contrasts focus on clinically defined bvFTD and report whole-brain results; this does not preclude inclusion given the review criteria. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria relevant to the meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the bvFTD-specific and whole-brain result criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (used VBM/tissue segmentation and VBM8 pipeline) and I5 (FTD patient group N=12 and controls N=18, both ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (FTD cases are reported without distinguishing subtypes — bvFTD or Pick's disease is not explicitly identified), I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing a bvFTD-only group to controls), I7 (no clearly identified group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results for a target bvFTD sample). No exclusion criteria from the list were triggered. Full text appears complete and provides methods/results/discussion.

This is an empirical VBM study (FSL-VBM) that includes a clearly defined bvFTD patient group (n=19) and healthy controls (n=25). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (>=6). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses and between-group contrasts versus controls with results provided in stereotactic (MNI) space (clusters and coordinates reported in Table 3 and supplement). It also reports bvFTD-specific whole-brain covariate analyses correlating caloric intake with gray matter atrophy (bvFTD not pooled with other patient groups). Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion requirements for the review objective of bvFTD imaging studies.

The study is excluded because, although it uses resting-state fMRI (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within a mixed FTD sample (I4), it does NOT meet key inclusion criteria required for this review. The bvFTD subgroup has only 4 participants (<6), failing I5. The paper does not report any between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD group to controls (bvFTD is pooled with other FTD subtypes), so I6 and I7 are not satisfied. The full text is complete and no exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Summary: inclusion criteria met: I3, I4; inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6, I7. No exclusion criteria applied.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It used FDG-PET imaging (I3) in a sample consisting exclusively of clinically diagnosed behavioral/frontal variant FTD patients (bvFTD) (I4). The overall patient sample (N=142) and PET subgroup (N=41) exceed the minimum required sample size, and healthy comparison groups (N=292 overall comparisons; N=16 for PET) meet the control size threshold (I5). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM analyses with results provided in stereotactic coordinates (MNI transformed to Talairach) for group contrasts between bvFTD patients and controls, and between haplotype-defined bvFTD subgroups, not pooled with other disorders (I6, I7). Results are presented as tables/figures with coordinates (I8). The provided full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion; it appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key target-sample and result-reporting inclusion criteria. Although it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and includes sufficient numbers in the FTD patient group (n=11) and controls (n=22) (I5), the paper does not explicitly identify a clinically-diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease subgroup (I4 is not clearly met—authors report ‘FTD’ without specifying bvFTD). Crucially, the study does not report a between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast explicitly comparing a bvFTD group to controls (I6 and I7 are not met); the primary VBM results are correlations across a mixed diagnostic sample, not group-level bvFTD vs control voxelwise contrasts. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest measurements (AC and SI thickness/area) from structural 3T MRI and provides no whole-brain voxelwise analyses or coordinate-based between-group contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia variant within the FTLD subgroup) and I5 (patient group n=7; control group n=16). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach or equivalent coordinate space), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results). The full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study uses VBM (I3) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts with MNI-like coordinates for a bvFTD clinical subgroup vs controls (I6, I7). It clearly includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) and presents whole-brain results in figures/text (I8). However, the paper does not explicitly report the number of bvFTD patients in the bvFTD subgroup in the provided full text (the overall sample is 18 patients but clinical-group counts are not specified in the text available here), so the required minimum patient-group size criterion (I5: ≥6 bvFTD participants) cannot be verified. No exclusion criteria from the review are met. Because a key numeric eligibility item (I5) cannot be confirmed from the provided full text, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

The full text reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=19) (I4) with a healthy control group (n=20) meeting the sample-size requirement (I5). The paper reports voxel-wise, whole-brain two-sample t-tests comparing each patient group (bvFTD and SD) to controls in standard space (MNI) (I6,I7); behavioural VBM correlations are also reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not restricted to non-qualifying modalities, and no comorbid psychiatric/substance confounds reported). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study is excluded because it does not provide the required between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; n=22), I5 (patient group size ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no reported between-group contrast of bvFTD versus controls in MNI/Talairach space; VBM analyses are within patient cohorts relating symptoms to grey matter, not bvFTD vs controls), I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD vs control comparison). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered (exclusion_criteria_applied = []). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Decision: EXCLUDED. Rationale: The study uses FDG-PET imaging and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise comparisons of an FTD group versus controls in Talairach space, with an adequate sample size (FTD n=13; controls n=26). However, the paper does not specify that the FTD sample comprises clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease, and the meta-analysis inclusion criterion I4 explicitly requires bvFTD or Pick's disease. Therefore it fails I4 and must be excluded. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I3 (FDG-PET), I5 (>=6 patients and controls), I6 (between-group voxelwise contrast in Talairach space for the FTD group vs controls), I7 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results for the FTD group), I8 (results presented/defined in text/figures). (c) Inclusion IDs NOT met: I4 (clinical diagnosis specifically of bvFTD or Pick's disease not clearly reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

Exclusion reason: E6 (only ROI/ no qualifying whole-brain between-group results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM, rs-fMRI, and FDG-PET), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, n=11), I5 (bvFTD group size ≥6). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD to healthy controls; study focuses on classification among patient groups rather than bvFTD vs controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly reported as coming from bvFTD vs controls). The full text appears complete. Therefore excluded because it does not provide the required whole-brain between-group voxelwise results for bvFTD vs controls.

This is an empirical VBM study of bvFTD using whole-brain voxelwise analyses. The paper uses voxel-based morphometry on T1-weighted MRI (preprocessed in CAT12/SPM12, normalized to MNI space), reports group-level VBM contrasts comparing 82 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients to 80 healthy controls with voxelwise results (FDR/FWE thresholds, cluster tables/figures referenced). Disease staging is specified and bvFTD is not pooled with other patient groups. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (reviews, ROI-only, non-empirical, seed-only FC/DTI/cortical thickness, or comorbid-sample issues) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and is eligible for inclusion.

The study is excluded because it fails inclusion criterion I5 (minimum sample size). Both bvFTD patient groups are N=5 (bvFTD(CBD)=5; bvFTD(Pick’s)=5), below the required >=6. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD / Pick’s patients), I6 (reports between-group contrasts in SPM5 with coordinate-based results), I7 (reports whole-brain voxelwise group results), I8 (reports results in tables/figures described in text). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (patient group sizes <6). Exclusion criteria applicable: none (E5,E6,E7,E8,E9 not met). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because imaging methods are surface-based cortical thickness analyses rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, which triggers exclusion criterion E9. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample; n=88 patients) and I5 (>=6 patients and >=6 controls; 88 patients, 30 controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (did not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in a defined stereotactic coordinate space such as MNI/Talairach — analyses are vertex/surface-based and coordinates/tables in stereotactic space are not provided), and I7 (while whole-brain surface maps are reported, the study does not provide voxelwise whole-brain results in a defined stochastic (MNI/Talairach) space required by the review). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical VBM study of patients clinically diagnosed with frontotemporal dementia (FTD) using Neary criteria; the overeating subgroup comprises 6 FTD patients (target bvFTD-like behavioral phenotype) and imaging analysis included voxel-wise contrasts versus 47 healthy controls and 21 nonovereating patients. The study uses VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed FTD/bvFTD patients (I4), has at least 6 patients in the target patient subgroup and sufficient controls (I5), reports between-group voxelwise contrasts in stereotactic coordinates (x,y,z) comparing the overeating FTD group to controls and non-overeaters (I6), and provides whole-brain voxelwise VBM results (thresholded and corrected within an a priori ROI) with figures and coordinates (I7,I8). Full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext_complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an rs-fMRI study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD with adequate sample sizes (41 bvFTD, 39 HC) and extensive network analyses. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (resting-state fMRI), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (≥6 patients and controls). However, the paper reports region-level (AAL parcellation) connectivity and MST-based graph metrics rather than voxelwise, whole-brain statistical contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach coordinates. Although images were registered to MNI space, no voxelwise between-group coordinate-based results are provided. Therefore it fails I6 and I7 and meets exclusion E6 (only ROI/region-based analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because, although it uses whole-brain VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within its symptomatic genetic groups (I4), and has adequate sample sizes (controls and patient subgroups exceed 6; I5), it does not report any between-group contrast in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) that directly compares a clinically defined bvFTD group to healthy controls (I6 not met). The voxelwise whole-brain results presented are for gene-by-clinical-status groups (e.g., C9orf72/GRN/MAPT presymptomatic vs symptomatic vs controls), not for a bvFTD diagnostic group per se, so there are no clearly identified whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results coming specifically from a bvFTD target sample (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis and is excluded.

This paper is a study protocol/description of an ongoing observational cohort (LOF study). Exclusion criteria met: E8 (non-empirical/methods-only paper without original results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET is included as an imaging modality in the protocol). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (participants are recruited based on late-onset frontal behavioral symptoms, not a clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s disease group), I5 (no reported bvFTD patient group size ≥6 is presented; the paper reports planned total cohort and expected FTD cases but no confirmed bvFTD group), I6 (no between-group voxelwise MNI/Talairach coordinates or contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls are reported), I7 (no reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise results). The manuscript lacks empirical group-level neuroimaging results required by the review (coordinates/voxelwise contrasts) and therefore must be excluded.

This is an empirical voxel-based morphometry (VBM) study that directly investigates cerebellar grey matter in bvFTD and related groups. It meets inclusion criteria: uses VBM (I3); includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (n=23) (I4); has adequate sample sizes for bvFTD and controls (23 bvFTD, 16 controls) (I5); reports between-group contrasts of bvFTD versus controls registered to MNI space with voxelwise, whole-brain results (FWE-corrected) (I6, I7); and presents results in figures/text (I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria were triggered (not a review, not ROI-only, not seed-based FC/DTI/thickness-only, and no evidence of disqualifying comorbid sample characteristics).

The study uses FDG-PET and VBM and includes clinically-diagnosed bvFTD patients and adequate sample sizes, but the primary whole-brain voxel-wise analyses compare MAPT mutation carriers (a group combining symptomatic bvFTD and asymptomatic carriers) to non-carriers. The paper does not report a whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level contrast that is exclusively between a clinically-defined bvFTD (symptomatic) group and controls; voxelwise comparisons among symptomatic carriers alone were not performed due to small AC sample and group-level contrasts by diagnostic subgroup were limited to ROI/z-score analyses. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I6 and I7 requiring at least one between-group voxelwise contrast in standard (MNI/Talairach) space comparing a bvFTD group (not pooled with other patient groups) to controls. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7. No exclusion criteria were triggered.

This study is excluded because it does not provide a whole-brain, group-level voxel-based morphometry (VBM) contrast comparing a clinically defined bvFTD group to healthy controls with stereotactic coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD and Pick's disease cases), and I5 (sufficient overall MRI sample sizes: 42 patients, 35 controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group contrast reported specifically for a bvFTD clinical group versus controls in MNI/Talairach space — VBM results are presented by pathological subgroups, not bvFTD syndromic group) and I7 (no whole-brain group-level result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target sample). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were triggered. The provided full text appears complete.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (behavioral-variant cases) and uses FDG-PET in a subset, it does not meet key imaging meta-analysis requirements. The paper presents descriptive imaging of a very small number of TBK1 carriers (FDG-PET in 2 patients; only five behavioral-variant FTD cases overall), and does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to healthy controls. There is no voxelwise statistical comparison or coordinate table for a bvFTD vs control contrast, nor a sufficiently large bvFTD patient group for meta-analytic inclusion. Therefore it fails I5 (sample size), I6 (between-group voxelwise contrast), and I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group result). Exclusion criterion E6 applies because the study provides no whole-brain voxelwise results (only individual/descriptive imaging findings). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET used) and I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients). Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6, I7. Full text is complete.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (SPM12) so it meets I3. However, it does not include a clinically diagnosed bvFTD (behavioral variant FTD) or Pick’s disease patient group as the target sample (I4 not met). Therefore there is no bvFTD vs control between-group contrast reported (I6 not met) and no whole-brain result specific to a bvFTD sample (I7 not met). The bvFTD-specific sample-size requirement (I5) is not applicable/satisfied because no bvFTD group is reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Conclusion: EXCLUDED because it does not address the target clinical group (bvFTD/Pick’s disease) and thus fails I4, I5 (for target group), I6, and I7, despite meeting I3.

This is an autopsy/case-series report of five symptomatic VT (vacuolar tauopathy) patients (plus two presymptomatic carriers). While the study includes FDG‑PET and other imaging in individual cases (satisfying I3) and the sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD cases with behavioral features (satisfying I4), it does not meet several mandatory inclusion criteria: I5 (patient group size >=6) is not met — only five symptomatic cases; I6 is not met — no between‑group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to controls reported in MNI/Talairach space; I7 is not met — no group‑level whole‑brain (voxelwise) results from the target sample. The paper presents descriptive, individual-level imaging and neuropathology rather than voxelwise group analyses or statistical contrasts vs controls. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria from the provided list directly apply.

Although this study uses resting-state fMRI (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (18 bvFTD cases; I4) with adequate patient group size (n=32; I5), and reports voxelwise coordinates/cluster results (I8), it does NOT report any between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls (i.e., no bvFTD-specific group vs control whole-brain contrast). The reported analyses are correlational (Reserve Index vs connectivity) within a mixed FTD sample and GRN+/- subgroups, and difference-of-slope comparisons between genetic subgroups, rather than a bvFTD vs control whole-brain contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria from the list apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=22) (I4) and healthy controls (n=38) with sample sizes ≥6 (I5), reports between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls with results localized in MNI space (I6), and provides whole-brain voxelwise VBM results identified as coming from the bvFTD group (I7). Results and coordinates are reported in main text and supplementary material (I8). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

EXCLUDED because the study does not report a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrast specifically comparing bvFTD patients (not pooled with other patient groups) to healthy controls. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (used VBM), I4 (included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients among the sample), I5 (sufficient sample sizes overall and per group appear >6), and I8 (whole-brain results are reported in figures/tables). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no reported between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach space directly comparing bvFTD group to controls without pooling across diagnoses) and I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target group). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not use any of the eligible imaging modalities (I3). It uses diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), arterial spin labeling (ASL) perfusion, and structural MRI (GM volume), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample present; n=9) and I5 (patient and control groups ≥6). The paper also reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses (TBSS) comparing bvFTD with controls, satisfying I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (required imaging modality) and I6 (study does not clearly report between-group results in a defined stereotactic coordinate space [MNI/Talairach] in the provided text; no coordinate table or coordinates are present). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered by the provided full text. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis because it fails the modality eligibility (I3).

This study is excluded because it does not match the imaging modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting requirements for the review and has an insufficient bvFTD sample size. Exclusion IDs met: E6 (study reports only ROI-based SBR and z-score analyses; no whole-brain voxelwise/MNI/Talairach coordinate results are reported). Inclusion IDs met: I4 (the sample includes a single FTLD/bvFTD case). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (imaging modality is 123I-FP-CIT SPECT, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I5 (bvFTD patient group <6 participants), I6/I7/I8 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinate tables/figures reported for a bvFTD vs control contrast). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the paper cannot be included in the meta-analysis.

The full text reports an empirical VBM study including 19 clinically-diagnosed bvFTD patients and 25 healthy controls (meets sample size). Whole-brain voxelwise VBM analyses were performed and group-level contrasts (bvFTD vs Controls) are reported; anatomical locations are provided in MNI stereotaxic space. The paper therefore meets imaging modality (I3), bvFTD sample (I4), sample size (I5), between-group MNI-coordinate contrasts (I6), whole-brain voxelwise results from the target group (I7), and acceptable reporting formats (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, no disallowed imaging modalities, and sample exclusions were standard). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, VBM coordinates described).

The study meets I3 (uses FDG-PET), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), and I5 (bvFTD sample >6 and controls ≥6). However, it does not clearly meet I6 and I7: the paper describes voxelwise FDG-PET comparisons between the overall FTLD group and controls and describes hypometabolic patterns for bvFTD subgroup, but it does not present a clear group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrast (with results in MNI/Talairach space or coordinate tables/figures) that specifically compares the bvFTD group versus controls where bvFTD is not pooled with other patient groups. Reported subgroup findings appear descriptive (per-patient or qualitative) and no coordinate-based whole-brain bvFTD>control contrast is provided in the full text supplied. Therefore it fails the requirement for a defined-stochastic-space between-group result for the target sample. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7. Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) .

This study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (8 bvFTD, 5 semantic dementia). However, although imaging was whole-brain VBM, the authors collapsed FTD subtypes and report group-level VBM results for FTD as a combined group rather than reporting a between-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast specifically comparing bvFTD alone to controls. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 (bvFTD-specific between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach space) and I7 (at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target group) are not met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM), I4 (bvFTD patients included), I5 (bvFTD n≥6 and controls n≥6), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria from the list (E5–E9) apply. Because the key requirement of bvFTD-specific whole-brain contrasts is not satisfied, the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain voxelwise result requirements. It uses manual region-of-interest cortical volumetry (not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), and it reports ROI-based volumetric and discriminant analyses without reporting any whole-brain voxelwise results in stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach). Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7 are not met. The study does meet I4 (includes clinically diagnosed FTD cases consistent with behavioral-variant descriptions) and I5 (sufficient sample sizes: FTD n=12, controls n=27). Exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) applies. Full text appears complete.

The full text is complete and shows the study used whole-brain VBM (satisfies I3), included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within the sample (47 bvFTD; satisfies I4), and had adequate sample sizes (96 patients, 34 controls; satisfies I5). However, the paper’s neuroimaging results are within-patient correlational VBM analyses (atrophy correlated with happiness behavior) performed on the combined FTD sample and do not present a between-group voxelwise contrast of bvFTD versus healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it does not meet I6 (no reported between-group bvFTD vs control contrast) nor I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Based on these missing inclusion criteria, the study should be excluded for this meta-analysis.

This full-text reports an empirical, voxelwise longitudinal structural MRI study of FTLD variants including a behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) group (n=44) and healthy controls (n=97). The methods use SPM/DARTEL and voxelwise Jacobian-derived change maps warped to MNI space and report group-level voxelwise contrasts (t-maps) between bvFTD and controls with consensus whole-brain change maps and figures. All inclusion criteria are satisfied: (I3) voxelwise morphometric MRI analysis (approach consistent with VBM-type whole-brain voxelwise morphometry), (I4) clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants included, (I5) sufficient sample sizes in patient and control groups, (I6) between-group contrasts in standardized (MNI) space comparing bvFTD vs controls (not pooled), (I7) group-level whole-brain voxelwise results presented, and (I8) results presented in figures/tables. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This full-text reports an empirical, voxelwise longitudinal structural MRI study of FTLD variants including a behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) group (n=44) and healthy controls (n=97). The methods use SPM/DARTEL and voxelwise Jacobian-derived change maps warped to MNI space and report group-level voxelwise contrasts (t-maps) between bvFTD and controls with consensus whole-brain change maps and figures. All inclusion criteria are satisfied: (I3) voxelwise morphometric MRI analysis (approach consistent with VBM-type whole-brain voxelwise morphometry), (I4) clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants included, (I5) sufficient sample sizes in patient and control groups, (I6) between-group contrasts in standardized (MNI) space comparing bvFTD vs controls (not pooled), (I7) group-level whole-brain voxelwise results presented, and (I8) results presented in figures/tables. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise FDG-PET analyses (SPM) comparing a clinically diagnosed frontal-variant FTD group to healthy controls with results reported in Talairach coordinates; sample sizes meet thresholds (22 patients, 15 controls). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and describes between-group contrasts and longitudinal within-group contrasts. Thus all required inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7,I8) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the paper does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing the bvFTD (frontal-variant FTD) group directly to healthy controls (Inclusion criterion I6 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET used), I4 (clinically diagnosed frontal-variant FTD, interpreted as bvFTD), I5 (patient N=70 ≥6), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise PCA maps reported for the patient group), I8 (results presented in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Because the meta-analysis requires at least one between-group contrast in stereotactic coordinates comparing bvFTD to controls, this study must be excluded.

Although this study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=58) with sufficient sample sizes and healthy controls (n=44), it does not report any between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrasts comparing the bvFTD group directly to controls. The VBM results are presented as brain–behavior correlations across a mixed sample of NDG patients and controls (and coatrophy checks parameterized diagnostic groups), rather than group-level voxelwise bvFTD vs. control contrasts in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 (between-group contrast bvFTD vs controls) and I7 (at least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group). Full text appears complete.

This full-text study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses VBM (I3); includes a clinical bvFTD subgroup (n=77) and healthy controls (n=136) (I4, I5); reports voxel-wise, whole-brain group-level comparisons between bvFTD and controls using MNI-based registration (I6, I7) and provides voxel/vertex results and downloadable regional and coordinate data in supplements (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, contains whole-brain voxelwise results, empirical original data, and includes VBM rather than only CT/DTI/seed-based FC). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and supplementary data availability).

Although this study uses whole-brain VBM (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=20) with an adequate control group (n=13) satisfying sample-size requirements (I4, I5), it does not report any between-group voxelwise contrast that directly compares the bvFTD group to healthy controls (i.e., a group-level bvFTD vs control contrast in MNI/Talairach space). The VBM results are reported as correlations across a pooled multi-diagnostic sample (sarcasm score regressions) with subsequent checks controlling for diagnosis; no unpooled, explicit bvFTD>control whole-brain contrasts or coordinates attributable solely to the bvFTD group are presented. Therefore the study fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7. Exclusion criteria: none met.

The full text shows VBM was used (I3), the sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=11) and controls (n=8) meeting the sample size requirement (I4,I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses by diagnostic group including bvFTD versus controls with significant clusters (e.g., lateral orbitofrontal gyrus, BA10) in Talairach space and cluster coordinates/sizes (I6,I7). Results are reported in text/tables/figures (I8). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

Exclusion based on lack of whole-brain voxelwise results. Exclusion criteria met: E6. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses FDG-PET), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (patient group size ≥6). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise/MNI or Talairach coordinate results comparing bvFTD to controls; assessments were visual ratings and diagnostic accuracy metrics), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported). Full text appears complete for decision-making.

This is an original empirical study that directly compares FDG-PET (and ASL-MRI) measures in a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample versus AD and cognitively normal controls. It reports voxel-wise, whole-brain group-level analyses (PLS logistic regression and voxel-wise GLMs with FDR correction) and presents spatial maps/figures separating bvFTD from controls and from AD. Sample sizes meet thresholds (bvFTD n=32; CN n=15). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an original empirical study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=30) with healthy controls (n=42). Imaging modalities include FDG-PET and voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses, and voxelwise diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) results spatially normalized to MNI space. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (ANCOVA/voxel-based DTI and VBM analyses) comparing bvFTD subgroups to controls and presents voxel-cluster results (figures/tables) clearly attributed to the target bvFTD sample. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and not limited to excluded modalities). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and violates none of the exclusion criteria. It is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the study does not meet key imaging and analysis inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample present, n=9) and I5 (patient group and control group sizes ≥6). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (imaging modality is 18F-THK5351 tau PET and 18F-florbetaben amyloid PET, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrast reported in a defined stereotactic space with MNI/Talairach coordinates), and I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results or coordinate tables provided; analyses are region/VOI-based). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (study reports only ROI/VOI analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper must be excluded from the review.

This is an empirical FDG-PET study of 52 patients who met Rascovsky criteria for probable bvFTD, using voxel-wise SPM analyses at single-subject and group levels compared to a normal image database (n=112). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise two-sample t-tests and conjunction analyses with proper SPM normalization (template-based) and FWE-corrected thresholds, clearly identifying frontal and temporo-limbic metabolic patterns and associated neuropsychological correlations. Full article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (FDG-PET), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD), I5 (>=6 patients and controls), I6 (between-group voxelwise contrasts in standard space), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), and I8 (results described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical neuroimaging study using voxelwise morphometry and FDG-PET (SPM-based VBM and FDG analyses). It includes an autopsy-confirmed PiD cohort with 8 patients who presented with bvFTD (meets bvFTD sample requirement) and 45 cognitively unimpaired controls. The study reports voxel-wise, whole-brain SPM12 group comparisons (bvFTD-PiD vs controls and PiD vs controls), with statistical maps corrected for multiple comparisons, indicating between-group results in a standardized template space. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; PET and MRI methods and group-level voxelwise results are presented. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the requirement that the patient sample is clinically diagnosed bvFTD (I4). Although it uses FDG-PET (I3) and has adequate sample sizes (13 FTLD patients; 10 controls; I5), the patient group is described as frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) without specification that they are behavioral-variant FTD or Pick’s disease. The meta-analysis requires results specifically from a clinically diagnosed bvFTD (or Pick’s) group and between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing that bvFTD group to controls (I6, I7). While the paper reports whole-brain voxelwise SPM comparisons for FTLD vs controls, these are not clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD-only sample, so I4, I6, and I7 are not satisfied. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is excluded because it does not meet key imaging and result-space criteria required by the review. It uses structural MRI morphometry (manual/Adaboost segmentation and radial distance surface mapping) rather than VBM, task/resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). Results are region-focused (putamen volume/shape) and do not report whole-brain voxelwise contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or coordinate tables — therefore it does not provide the required between-group voxelwise coordinates for bvFTD vs controls (I6 and I7 not met). The sample does include clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (I4 met) with adequate group sizes (FTD n=33, controls n=17; I5 met). Because the paper reports ROI-only analyses without whole-brain results, exclusion criterion E6 applies. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This full text meets all required inclusion criteria for the bvFTD imaging meta-analysis. It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality (I3). The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (18 bvFTD among 40 FTD patients) (I4) and has adequate sample sizes (bvFTD n=18; controls n=27) (I5). The paper reports between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls with results reported in MNI coordinates (e.g., x=8,y=28,z=-28) and FWE-corrected group atrophy maps (I6, I7, I8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met: this is an empirical VBM study with whole-brain results (E5, E6, E8, E9 not applicable; no evidence of disallowed comorbid samples per text)

This study is excluded because the imaging modality is surface-based cortical thickness and volumetric segmentation using FreeSurfer rather than VBM, FDG-PET, or fMRI (thus failing I3). It meets inclusion criteria I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (bvFTD sample n=37 and controls n=33, both >6), and I7 (reports whole-brain vertex-wise cortical thickness analyses). It does not meet I3 (required imaging modalities) and does not appear to provide between-group results in a standard stereotactic coordinate space (MNI/Talairach) for voxelwise contrasts (I6 not met). Exclusion criterion E9 applies (study reports cortical thickness methods rather than accepted modalities). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The study uses FDG-PET (I3 satisfied) but does not provide results specific to clinically-diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease. The FTLD subgroup includes only N=13 with FTD=3, which is likely too small and not clearly identified as bvFTD, so I4 not satisfied and I5 not satisfied (bvFTD-specific group <6). The paper does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing a bvFTD group to controls with the bvFTD group unpooled (I6 not satisfied). Although whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported, these are not clearly identified as coming from a target bvFTD sample (I7 not satisfied). No exclusion criteria from the provided list are clearly met. Full text appears complete. Conclusion: exclude because target-sample-related inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7) are not met despite appropriate imaging modality (I3).

Full text is complete. Imaging modalities satisfy I3 (VBM/MRI and FDG-PET used). Sample sizes satisfy I5 (FTLD n=11; controls n=13). However, the FTLD group is a pooled sample (FTD n=4, SD n=5, mixed n=2) and the paper does not report group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrasts or coordinate results specifically for a behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease group that are separate from other FTLD subtypes. Therefore I4 (explicit bvFTD/Pick’s group), I6 (between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls without pooling), and I7 (group-level whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from the target bvFTD sample) are not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Because the target of the meta-analysis is bvFTD and this study does not provide isolated whole-brain results for a bvFTD-only group, it must be excluded.

The study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as an imaging modality (I3), has adequate group sizes (bvFTD n=25; controls n=37) (I5), and reports between-group contrasts with coordinates in MNI stereotaxic space (I6). However, the analyses were performed using an ROI mask focused on motor-system regions (methods state an ROI mask was created and ROI analyses conducted), and the paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) result for the bvFTD group. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7 and meets exclusion criterion E6 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Hence the study is excluded.

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically-diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=90 with MRI) with age-matched controls (n=44). The paper uses voxel-based morphometry (SPM/VBM) as the imaging modality and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (VBM T-maps, family-wise error corrected) comparing bvFTD subgroups to controls (Figure 2B; methods state SPM8 normalization implying MNI space). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (both patient and control groups ≥6). Whole-brain results are presented in figures and described in the text; thus results are available in a defined stereotactic space. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only, seed-FC/DTI-only, non-empirical) are met. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided.

This study should be excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI) structural MRI volumetric analyses (Freesurfer-derived regional volumes) rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET voxelwise whole-brain analyses.
