Exclusion IDs met: E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion IDs met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; n=48) and I5 (sample sizes meet minimum: bvFTD n=48, controls n=94). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (imaging modality is Freesurfer ROI volumetry, not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrasts reported in stereotactic space/MNI or Talairach), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported). The full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper does not satisfy the review’s imaging and whole-brain reporting inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

This study used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reported voxelwise group comparisons (MAPT and GRN mutation groups vs. controls) in stereotactic space. The MAPT group (n=11) presented initially with behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD), and the GRN group (n=9) included bvFTD cases; healthy controls n=15. All patient groups meet the minimum sample size. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (cross-sectional VBM and longitudinal voxel-wise analyses) clearly identified for the mutation groups (including the MAPT group that presented with bvFTD) and provides maps/analyses in MNI space. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and not using only excluded modalities). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; sufficient for screening.

Full text is complete. The study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within its cohort (I4). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (42 patients, 30 controls) (I5). However, the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrast that is specifically and exclusively comparing a bvFTD patient group to controls; all whole-brain VBM results are reported for pathologically defined FTLD-TDP subtypes (types 1–3) rather than a bvFTD-only group. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 (a between-group contrast comparing bvFTD group to controls where bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups) and I7 (a whole-brain, voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the target bvFTD sample). No exclusion criteria from the review’s list are met. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because key inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not satisfied.

Excluded because study does not meet key inclusion criteria for the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses 18F-FDG PET) and I5 (patient group size ≥6; FTLD N=31). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (does not specify clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD or Picks disease — sample is labeled FTLD without bvFTD-specific reporting), I6 (no between-group whole-brain contrast in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD target group). No exclusion criteria from the list (E5–E9) directly apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore exclude.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain reporting inclusion criteria. It uses manual ROI-based hypothalamic volumetry on structural MRI (not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) and reports ROI results rather than whole-brain, voxelwise coordinates in a standard space. Therefore it violates inclusion criteria I3, I6, I7, and I8 and meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). The study does satisfy I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients) and I5 (bvFTD n=19; controls n=23). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study meets inclusion criteria for the review. It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) with group sizes well above the minimum (30 C9-positive, 30 C9-negative; controls N=30) (I5). The authors performed whole-brain, voxelwise VBM analyses registered to MNI152 and report group-level contrasts versus controls (I6, I7), with results presented in figures and tables and supplementary bvFTD-only analyses (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is empirical (not a review), reports whole-brain VBM (not ROI-only), and excludes participants with comorbid psychiatric, other neurodegenerative disorders, or substance abuse per methods. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This empirical study uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes a clinically defined frontotemporal dementia (FTD) subgroup characterized by behavioral/personality changes consistent with bvFTD (I4). Sample sizes meet minimums: 17 FTLD patients (including an FTD subgroup) and 9 controls (I5). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM analyses and group comparisons of FTD and SD versus controls (FTD vs. controls contrasts reported), using spatial normalization to a standard template (i.e., results in stereotaxic space), satisfying between-group contrast reporting requirements (I6). Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results are described in the text and figures/tables (SPM voxelwise thresholds), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement (I7) and acceptable reporting formats (I8). No exclusion criteria apply: this is not a review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, not limited to excluded modalities, and there is no evidence of disqualifying comorbid psychiatric/neurological sample issues. Full text appears to contain core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an FDG-PET whole-brain study (I3 satisfied) including a mixed cohort of early dementias with an FTLD subgroup. However, the paper does not provide data specific to behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD)/Pick’s disease at the group level: the FTLD subgroup includes only 3 patients labelled 'FTD' (n=3, <6), and reported group-level contrasts are for pooled FTLD (and AD) versus subjective cognitive impairment rather than a bvFTD-specific between-group contrast. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I4 (bvFTD/Pick’s disease sample reported as target group), I5 (at least 6 patients in target patient group), I6 (bvFTD-specific between-group contrasts in standard space), and I7 (a whole-brain group-level result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD/bvFTD-only sample). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered by this study. Full text appears complete. Because the review requires bvFTD-specific, group-level whole-brain coordinates with adequate sample size, this study is excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise (MNI/Talairach) between-group results comparing bvFTD to controls. Although it includes resting-state fMRI (I3), clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), and sufficient sample sizes (I5), the analyses are ROI-based functional connectivity and tract-specific DTI measures (no voxelwise coordinates or whole-brain statistical maps). Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. Exclusion criteria E6 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and E9 (reports DTI and seed/ROI-based FC methods rather than acceptable modalities) apply. Given these methodological limitations relative to the meta-analysis requirements, the paper must be excluded.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality, included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (N=23) and a healthy control group (N=20), and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise VBM results (two-sample t-test comparing bvFTD to controls) and voxelwise regression analyses linking behavioral measures to GM volume. The paper provides whole-brain results (group comparison and regressions) that are clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD sample and refers to figures/tables/supplementary materials for results/coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply: it is an empirical study (not a review), reports whole-brain analyses (not ROI-only), does not use only seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness, and there is no indication of disqualifying comorbid psychiatric/substance/other-dementia samples. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, discussion and imaging details; supplementary tables are referenced. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion.

This study meets several inclusion criteria: it used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (22 patients) and age-matched controls (22) satisfying sample-size requirements (I4, I5), and reports between-group voxelwise contrasts after registration to MNI space (I6). However, the neuroimaging analyses were conducted within a predefined fronto-subcortical region-of-interest mask rather than as an unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise analysis. The paper does not present an unmasked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise result from the target sample; therefore it does not meet the whole-brain evidence requirement (I7). Because the study reports only ROI-restricted voxelwise results, it falls under the exclusion criterion E6 (studies that report only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Conclusion: EXCLUDED (meets E6; satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6; does not satisfy I7).

Full text is complete. The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and includes FTD patients (FTD n=15, SD n=10) with adequate sample sizes and controls, so I3, I4 and I5 are met. However, the VBM whole-brain contrasts are reported for pooled FTLD (FTD+SD) versus controls rather than for behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD/FTD) alone. The review requires group-level whole-brain contrasts that come specifically from the target bvFTD group and not pooled with other patient groups (I6 and I7). This study does not report bvFTD-only whole-brain voxelwise results (FTD-specific VBM contrasts are not presented), so it fails I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered.

The study uses FDG-PET (I3 met), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants within the FTD sample (I4 met), and has adequate sample sizes (48 bvFTD; 73 controls) meeting I5. However, all voxelwise, whole-brain group analyses are reported for the pooled 'FTD' group (48 bvFTD + 14 svPPA) versus controls; the paper does not present a between-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast specifically for the bvFTD subgroup versus controls. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (bvFTD-specific between-group contrast reported in stereotactic space and at least one group-level whole-brain result from the target sample) are not met. No exclusion criteria from the provided list apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Result: EXCLUDED because bvFTD-specific whole-brain voxelwise results are not reported.

While the study uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed FTD group (Neary criteria) with n=17 (I4, I5), it does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (e.g., in MNI or Talairach space) comparing the FTD/bvFTD group to controls. Results focus on per-subject 3D-SSP maps and diagnostic accuracy (sensitivity/specificity) rather than coordinate-based, whole-brain group contrasts. Therefore it fails I6 and I7. Because no whole-brain group voxelwise results are reported (only subject-level maps/volumes-of-interest and diagnostic metrics), exclusion criterion E6 applies. Full text appears complete.

This study used FDG-PET (I3) and had adequate patient group sizes (I5: FTLD n=11, AD n=11, CVD n=9). However, it does not explicitly state that the FTLD group comprises clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD or Pick’s disease (I4 not clearly met). Critically, the imaging results are reported as regional ROI z-scores and qualitative regional hypometabolism (e.g., temporoparietal, bifrontal) rather than stereotactic, voxelwise whole-brain coordinates (no MNI/Talairach coordinates or voxelwise maps reported). Therefore the study does not provide the required between-group voxelwise contrasts in standard space (I6/I7/I8 not met) and instead meets exclusion E6 (ROI-only/no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical VBM study including a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=11) and controls (n=15), and reports voxelwise between-group results in MNI space; however, all VBM analyses were conducted within a prefrontal/striatal ROI mask rather than as whole-brain voxelwise analyses. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD sample present), I5 (patient and control groups ≥6), I6 (between-group contrasts reported in MNI space for bvFTD vs controls). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise result for the target sample; analyses were ROI-restricted). Exclusion criterion met: E6 (reports only ROI-restricted analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails I7 and meets E6.

Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study used voxel-based morphometry), I4 (bvFTD patients included, n=18), I5 (bvFTD and control groups exceed n≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD group directly to controls in MNI/Talairach coordinates is reported in the provided full text—the VBM results are reported as brain–behavior correlations across the full cohort rather than a bvFTD vs. HC contrast), and I7 (no clearly identified group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result specifically reported as coming from the bvFTD group is provided in the text/tables as presented). Exclusion criteria met: none (no ROI-only restriction, not a review, no disallowed modality). Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the paper is excluded because it does not report the required between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast for the bvFTD group vs controls (I6/I7 not satisfied).

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses resting-state fMRI (ICA/dual regression) as an imaging modality (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group (n=12) (I4) with matched healthy controls (n=17) and patient group sizes exceed the minimum of 6 (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (Randomize/TBSS) with between-group contrasts including bvFTD vs controls (not pooled with other diagnoses) and refers to cluster/ supplement tables for results (I6, I7, I8). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary tables are referenced for coordinates/cluster information. No exclusion criteria apply (no review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and the sample exclusions reported mean comorbid psychiatric/neurological/substance cases were excluded). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the bvFTD meta-analysis.

The study includes resting-state fMRI and VBM-based structural MRI (I3). It explicitly includes clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD patients (bvFTD) within the sample (bvFTD n=41) and matched cognitively normal controls (n=100), satisfying sample size requirements (I4, I5). The paper reports syndrome-specific group comparisons (typical bvFTD subgroup versus cognitively normal) with mean atrophy maps and group-level (syndrome – cognitively normal) alterations derived from voxelwise W-score maps in MNI space and corresponding functional connectivity contrasts (I6, I7). Results are presented across figures and supplementary materials and source data are available, meeting the acceptable reporting formats (I8). No exclusion criteria (reviews, ROI-only, seed-only FC, DTI-only, or other disqualifying features) were triggered. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Supplementary information).

This is an empirical study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=14) and age-matched controls (n=19). Imaging modalities include voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and resting-state and task-based fMRI; VBM and voxelwise resting-state group comparisons are reported. Sample sizes meet the ≥6 requirement for patients and controls. The paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts (VBM comparison of bvFTD vs controls; resting-state connectivity differences) with peak coordinates provided (e.g., left ATL [−45,13,−37], left IFG [−52,2,14]), and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are clearly described. Full text content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Figures, coordinates) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; no disqualifying comorbid sample; not non-empirical; not limited to seed FC/DTI/cortical thickness only). Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=19) and healthy controls (n=20). Imaging modality used is task fMRI (I3). The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (I4) with group sizes exceeding the minimum (I5). The paper reports voxel-wise whole-brain group comparisons (faces vs scrambles) with a significant cluster in the left caudate nucleus described in the text and shown in figures (I6, I7). Results are presented in standard stereotactic space and/or detailed in text/figures, which is acceptable reporting (I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references (fulltext_complete). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=35) and uses resting-state fMRI (satisfying I3, I4, I5), its imaging analyses are connectome/parcellation- and network-based (220-region parcellation, DTI-based structural connectome, NBS, and region/edge-level distribution analyses). The paper does not present any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results reported in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) nor coordinate tables for bvFTD vs controls. Therefore it does not meet I6 or I7 (no between-group voxelwise coordinates in defined stereotactic space and no whole-brain voxelwise group result). This qualifies as a study reporting only region/ROI-based/connectomic results, triggering exclusion criterion E6. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7. Exclusion criteria applied: E6 (only ROI/region-level, no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it used Voxel-Based Morphometry (I3), included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (ALS-FTD patients who met bvFTD criteria) (I4), had sufficient sample sizes (ALS-FTD n=7; controls n=24) (I5), reported between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing the bvFTD (ALS-FTD) group to controls using standard neuroanatomical space and SPM/VBM methods (I6), and provided whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (VBM and TBSS) clearly attributed to the ALS-FTD group (I7,I8). Full text is complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion decision because required between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD patients to controls are not reported. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET used), I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed behavioral phenotypes / bvFTD cases—25/39 predominant behavioral), I5 (bvFTD subgroup size ≥6). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrast in stereotactic space comparing bvFTD to controls where bvFTD is not pooled), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target group). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Because I6 and I7 are required and not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

Although this study used task-based fMRI and voxel-based morphometry (I3) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) with sufficient sample size (bvFTD n=10 overall; imaging subset bvFTD n=7) meeting the sample-size criterion (I5), it does not report any whole-brain, between-group voxelwise contrast comparing a bvFTD-only group to controls in MNI/Talairach space. The structural (VBM) imaging results reported in the paper combine bvFTD and PNFA into a single patient group for the between-group VBM contrasts, and the task fMRI was conducted only in healthy young adults. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (bvFTD-only whole-brain between-group results) are not met. No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete.

This study used VBM and included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=22) and healthy controls (n=21), satisfying imaging and sample-size criteria. However, it does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts directly comparing the bvFTD group to controls in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The VBM analyses reported are correlation/regression analyses within the patient cohort and within the bvFTD subgroup (behaviour–anatomy correlations), not bvFTD versus control voxelwise group contrasts; whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed but yielded no significant between-group results. Therefore the study fails inclusion criteria I6 (no between-group bvFTD vs control contrast in stereotactic space) and I7 (no reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise result identified as from the bvFTD group).

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within its sample, and has sufficient total patient (n=15) and control (n=12) group sizes. However, the paper does not report any between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrasts that isolate a bvFTD-only group versus controls in MNI or Talairach space. Reported whole-brain VBM results are for the combined FTD group versus controls and for FTD subgroupings (fast vs slow acquisition), but bvFTD is not analyzed or reported separately. Therefore it fails to meet I6 and I7 required for inclusion in this bvFTD-focused meta-analysis.

Excluded because the study does not meet the imaging and whole-brain reporting inclusion criteria. The paper used structural MRI with FreeSurfer ROI volumetric analyses (not VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET), so I3 is not met. It did not report any whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts in stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) space, so I6 and I7 are not met. This matches exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample present, N=10) and I5 (patient and control group sizes ≥6). Full text appears complete.

While this study meets several inclusion criteria (uses voxel-based morphometry [I3], includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants [I4], and has adequate sample sizes in patient and control groups [I5]), it does NOT report a whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrast in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing a bvFTD group to controls where the bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups. The main VBM analyses relate to (a) presence of ‘disgusting behaviors’ across a heterogeneous patient sample and (b) ROI analyses restricted to the insula within bvFTD/svPPA. There is no clear group-level whole-brain voxelwise result identified as coming specifically from a bvFTD vs control contrast, so criteria I6 and I7 are not satisfied. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical study that used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses to compare clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) patients (n=19) to healthy controls (n=20). The paper reports voxelwise between-group contrasts and behavioral–neuroimaging correlations with MNI coordinates and cluster results (whole-brain, voxelwise VBM with tables/figures), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, group-level results. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, no prohibited imaging modality, and participants without concurrent psychiatric/other dementia conditions). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary material availability noted but not required. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical FDG-PET study of clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD patients (bvFTD) with matched controls. Imaging modality: FDG-PET (meets I3). Sample: 21 bvFTD patients (15 men, 6 women) and 30 controls (FDG-PET available for 12 controls) satisfying minimum sample size (meets I4 and I5). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level SPM analyses in standard space (MNI) including between-group contrasts (patients vs controls) and parametric voxelwise regressions within the bvFTD group relating hypometabolism to behavioral scores; results are reported with coordinates and FWE-corrected thresholds (meets I6, I7, I8). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; not a review and does not rely solely on ROIs or excluded modalities. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study fulfills all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This full text meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (12 patients) and healthy controls (20) (I4, I5), reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM analyses registered to MNI space with group contrasts between bvFTD and controls (I6, I7), and results are presented in the main text/figures (I8). The paper is empirical, not a review, and does not violate exclusion criteria (no ROI-only reporting, no seed-based FC/DTI-only methods, no psychiatric comorbidity exclusions). The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods (including VBM), Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore include.

The paper uses FDG-PET (I3) in a sample of clinically diagnosed frontal variant/bvFTD patients (fv-FTD; I4) with 13 patients and 21 controls (I5). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM correlations between AM scores and FDG-Uptake within the fv-FTD group and provides coordinate-based localization (Talairach/MNI transformations) (I7, I8). However, it does not present any between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrasts directly comparing the bvFTD/fv-FTD group to controls in MNI/Talairach space, so inclusion criterion I6 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants) and I5 (sample sizes: bvFTD n=57 and controls n=172 exceed minimum). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 — imaging modality is structural T1 volumetry/parcellation and SuStaIn regional volumetric analysis, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET; I6 and I7 — the paper reports region/parcel/cluster-level volumetric comparisons and SuStaIn-derived maps, not group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (only ROI/parcel-based analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study uses voxel-based, whole-brain pattern analysis of structural MRI (RAVENS/voxel-based methods) and includes 12 FTD patients (of whom 8 had behavioral/executive-predominant presentations), and 12 matched controls. However, the FTD patients and subtypes were pooled together for all reported voxelwise/group-level contrasts; the paper does not report a bvFTD-specific between-group voxelwise contrast (i.e., bvFTD not analyzed/reported separately from other FTD subtypes), nor are results clearly reported specifically for a bvFTD-only group in stereotactic coordinates. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 requiring bvFTD-specific, whole-brain voxelwise results (in defined stereotactic space) that are not pooled with other patient groups. Included: I3 (voxel-based morphometry/voxel-wise structural MRI methods), I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within the FTD group), I5 (patient and control groups >=6). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) . Because bvFTD-specific whole-brain voxelwise contrasts are not provided, the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria and is excluded.

This study used FDG-PET and included 8 FTD patients, but it does not specify that participants are behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease, and the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing a bvFTD group to controls. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I4, I6, and I7. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET used), I5 (≥6 patients). No exclusion criteria from the list (E5–E9) were directly triggered by the text; exclusion is due to unmet inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, two-center MRI study that uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise comparisons in MNI space. It includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=24) and healthy controls (n=37), meeting the minimum sample size. The paper presents group-level whole-brain VBM and TBSS (DTI) results for bvFTD versus controls and bvFTD versus AD, with voxelwise statistical results and describes ROIs derived from those voxelwise contrasts; results are clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (systematic review/meta-analysis only, ROI-only, non-empirical, or exclusive use of disallowed modalities) are met.

Excluded based on E6 (ROI-only analyses). The study uses structural MRI with FreeSurfer-derived lobar/ROI measures (cortical GM and T1-hypointense WMSA) rather than VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). The sample consists of genetic pre-dementia GRN+ and C9orf72+ carriers and non-carrier family members, not clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick's disease patients (I4 not met). Sample size criterion is met (I5: GRN+ N=10, C9orf72+ N=23, non-carriers N=49). The study does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results or stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) comparing a clinically defined bvFTD group to controls (I6 and I7 not met). Full text appears complete. Therefore it fails required imaging-modality and whole-brain reporting inclusion criteria and is excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not use the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) and does not report whole-brain voxelwise group-level results in a standard stereotactic space. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample) and I5 (≥6 patients in the MRI subgroup and ≥6 controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (study uses structural volumetry/FreeSurfer and BSI, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrast results reported in MNI/Talairach stereotactic coordinates), and I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result from the target bvFTD sample). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (reports region-based/volumetric analyses and individual deformation maps, but lacks whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This full-text study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses VBM (I3); includes a clinical bvFTD subgroup (n=77) and healthy controls (n=136) (I4, I5); reports voxel-wise, whole-brain group-level comparisons between bvFTD and controls using MNI-based registration (I6, I7) and provides voxel/vertex results and downloadable regional and coordinate data in supplements (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, contains whole-brain voxelwise results, empirical original data, and includes VBM rather than only CT/DTI/seed-based FC). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and supplementary data availability).

This full-text study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses VBM (I3); includes a clinical bvFTD subgroup (n=77) and healthy controls (n=136) (I4, I5); reports voxel-wise, whole-brain group-level comparisons between bvFTD and controls using MNI-based registration (I6, I7) and provides voxel/vertex results and downloadable regional and coordinate data in supplements (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, contains whole-brain voxelwise results, empirical original data, and includes VBM rather than only CT/DTI/seed-based FC). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and supplementary data availability).

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinical bvFTD subgroup (n=64) and a healthy control group (n=32). The authors performed whole-brain voxel-based morphometry analyses (SPM8) and report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise comparisons of each clinical phenotype versus controls (see Supplementary Figure 1) as well as whole-brain correlations of clinical scales within the bvFTD group. Imaging modality (VBM), adequate sample sizes, and whole-brain voxelwise results clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD subgroup satisfy the review’s inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not DTI/FC-only, and comorbid psychiatric/other-dementia cases were excluded per methods). Although coordinate tables are not shown in the supplied text, results are reported in figures/supplementary material and described in the text, which is acceptable under the protocol.

Although the study uses VBM and resting-state fMRI and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases with adequate sample sizes, the analyses combine bvFTD and avPPA into a single FTD-GRN+ group and do not report any voxelwise between-group contrasts specifically comparing a bvFTD-only group to controls. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (no bvFTD-specific whole-brain contrasts reported). Full text appears complete.

The study is task-based fMRI with 7 FTD patients and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses with Talairach coordinates (meets I3, I5, I7, I8). However, it does not explicitly state that patients had behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) per inclusion criterion I4, and crucially it does not report between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space as required by I6; the reported contrasts are FTD vs AD. No exclusion criteria were triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I4 (uncertain/specification of bvFTD) and I6 (no bvFTD vs control whole-brain contrast).

This study reports resting-state fMRI analysis in a sample that includes a clearly defined bvFTD patient group (n=42) and healthy controls (n=52). Imaging modality is rs-fMRI (satisfies I3). The bvFTD group is clinically diagnosed and reported separately (I4). Patient and control group sizes exceed the minimum of 6 (I5). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain analyses (parcel-wise across a 400-parcel Schaefer atlas) with mixed-effects between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD versus controls (not pooled) and presents cortical surface maps and statistical comparisons (satisfies I6 and I7). Results are reported in text and figures (acceptable per I8). No exclusion criteria are met: this is an original empirical rs-fMRI study (not a review), not ROI-only or seed-only, and does not have disqualifying comorbid samples. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion provided). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review objective focused on bvFTD resting-state imaging.

This study is excluded because it does not use the required imaging modalities or report whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts in stereotactic space. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (only ROI analyses, no whole-brain voxelwise results) and E9 (uses cortical thickness/FreeSurfer ROI volumetry rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinical bvFTD sample present; 152 bvFTD cases) and I5 (≥6 patients in the bvFTD group). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (did not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no reported between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls), and I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result reported). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study is excluded because it does not provide a whole-brain, group-level voxel-based morphometry (VBM) contrast comparing a clinically defined bvFTD group to healthy controls with stereotactic coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD and Pick's disease cases), and I5 (sufficient overall MRI sample sizes: 42 patients, 35 controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group contrast reported specifically for a bvFTD clinical group versus controls in MNI/Talairach space — VBM results are presented by pathological subgroups, not bvFTD syndromic group) and I7 (no whole-brain group-level result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target sample). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were triggered. The provided full text appears complete.

The study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses resting-state fMRI (I3) alongside multimodal imaging and surface-based morphometry; includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (N=19) (I4) and control groups with sample sizes >6 (I5); reports between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls) and whole-brain, voxelwise results (e.g., "p < .05, whole-brain FDR-corrected" for structural correlations and group FC differences) which are clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group (I6, I7). The paper refers to supplementary materials (coordinates/figures) online, making coordinate reporting acceptable (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: this is an empirical original study (not a review), contains whole-brain analyses (not ROI-only), and does not rely solely on seed-based FC or cortical-thickness methods. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore, include for the meta-analysis focused on bvFTD imaging studies.

This study uses VBM (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (behavioral/dysexecutive FTD subtype) with n=14 and controls n=20 (I4, I5). However, it does not report a voxelwise between-group contrast comparing bvFTD (FTD) patients vs. controls as an isolated patient group in MNI/Talairach space; VBM results are correlations across combined groups and the authors explicitly combined FTLD subtypes for VBM rather than presenting a separate whole-brain group-level contrast for the behavioral-variant FTD subgroup. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (no between-group bvFTD vs control voxelwise result and no clear group-level whole-brain result coming from bvFTD alone). No exclusion criteria from the review (E5–E9) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Although this is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with adequate sample sizes, it does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD patients to healthy controls in standard stereotactic space. The MRI/VBM analyses are correlations of grey matter with task performance conducted within the patient group (MRI available for 16 patients); controls did not contribute to whole-brain between-group VBM contrasts. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (between-group contrast bvFTD vs controls in MNI/Talairach space) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (>=6 patients and controls), I7 (reports at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result from the target sample). No exclusion criteria were triggered.

This study should be excluded because, although it uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes frontotemporal lobar degeneration patients with a behavioral-variant subgroup (35 bvFTD patients) satisfying the bvFTD sample requirement (I4) and has adequate patient and control group sizes (I5), it does not report whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts in a standard stereotactic space specific to the bvFTD subgroup. Analyses are based on region-of-interest/parcellation (AAL VOIs) and metabolic connectivity patterns rather than voxelwise MNI/Talairach coordinate contrasts; the FTLD analyses are reported at the group (FTLD) level rather than separately for bvFTD. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met, and exclusion criterion E6 (studies that report only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) applies. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7. Exclusion criteria met: E6.

This is an empirical VBM study (FSL–VBM in MNI space) that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=18) and age/education-matched healthy controls (n=28). Whole-brain, voxelwise analyses are reported (including covariate analyses and group comparisons) with results clearly identified for the bvFTD group (e.g., VBM correlations of IGT modified net score within bvFTD). Imaging methods specify MNI152 registration. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; core data appear complete. Therefore the study meets the imaging modality (VBM), target diagnosis (bvFTD), sample size thresholds, and reports whole-brain group-level voxelwise results in a defined stereotactic space.

This empirical study includes clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (N=13) and healthy controls (N=19), exceeding the minimum group sizes. It reports whole-brain voxelwise structural analyses (VBM using VBM8/DARTEL) and resting-state fMRI analyses (fALFF), satisfying the imaging modality requirement. Group-level between-group contrasts and voxelwise regression results are reported and described with MNI coordinates (e.g., ‘‘Z‐coordinates in MNI space’’) for comparisons involving the bvFTD group (not pooled with other patient groups). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing verification of criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, no disallowed modalities, no comorbid sample issues reported). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is eligible for the review.

The full text reports an empirical MRI study that includes voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (I3). The sample includes 13 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (part of the FTLD sample) and 19 controls, meeting the minimum group sizes (I4, I5). The paper presents whole-brain, voxel-wise group comparisons of bvFTD versus controls after spatial normalization to standard space (MNI) with statistical parametric maps and figures, satisfying between-group contrasts in defined stochastic space and whole-brain results (I6, I7, I8). The full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply.

The full text reports a voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain, voxelwise analysis including a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=14) and healthy controls (n=28). Between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls) are reported and displayed in MNI space with voxelwise statistics (FWE-corrected), satisfying group-level whole-brain results. Sample sizes for patient and control groups exceed the minimum of 6. The paper uses VBM (I3), includes bvFTD patients (I4), meets sample size requirements (I5), reports between-group MNI-space contrasts specific to bvFTD (I6), provides whole-brain voxelwise results for the target group (I7), and presents results in figures/tables/supplementary material (I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The study is EXCLUDED. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses voxel-based morphometry/structural MRI VBM analyses) and I5 (patient group FTLD n=55 and controls n=73, both >6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the sample does not specify clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD or Pick’s disease; cases are pathologically defined FTLD subtypes without clear clinical bvFTD grouping), I6 and I7 (the paper does not report a whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrast specifically comparing a clinically defined bvFTD group to controls in MNI/Talairach space). Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were triggered. Therefore the study does not meet the review requirement of reporting whole-brain voxelwise results for a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group and is excluded.

The study uses resting-state fMRI (meets I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (7 bvFTD cases within the sample; meets I4), and has adequate group sizes (patient subgroup n=7 and controls n≥6; meets I5). However, all reported voxelwise whole-brain analyses are performed on the pooled FTD-GRN+ group (14 FTD-GRN+ comprising 7 bvFTD + 7 avPPA) versus controls. The paper does not report any between-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast that isolates the bvFTD subgroup alone compared to controls, nor coordinate-based/binary results clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD-only group. Therefore it fails I6 and I7, which require bvFTD-specific, whole-brain between-group voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Consequently the study must be excluded for not providing bvFTD-specific whole-brain results.

This is an empirical multimodal MRI study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=20) and matched healthy controls (n=20). It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) for whole-brain GM analyses (reported with cluster maxima coordinates) and reports voxelwise between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls in MNI space. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6) for both patients and controls. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are clearly reported for the target bvFTD group (text, statistical maps, and coordinates). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only, seed-based FC/DTI-only, or samples with disallowed comorbidities) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it uses resting-state fMRI (alongside other MRI modalities) (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=27) (I4); has sufficient sample sizes for patient and control groups (bvFTD n=27; controls n=48) (I5); reports between-group contrasts using standard-space analyses (MNI) comparing bvFTD to controls and to EOAD (voxelwise dual-regression and TBSS analyses) (I6); presents group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) results for the target sample (I7); and these whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures/supplementary materials as described (I8). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and supplementary indications) is provided and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only analyses, seed-only FC/DTI-only/cortical-thickness-only reporting) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study examines presymptomatic C9ORF72 expansion carriers (no clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), so it does not meet the requirement that the sample include clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease patients (I4). It therefore also fails the meta-analysis requirement to report between-group contrasts comparing a bvFTD patient group to controls (I6). The paper does meet several methodological criteria: it uses VBM and resting-state fMRI (I3), includes adequate sample sizes (preSxC9 n=15; controls >6) (I5), reports whole-brain voxelwise results (I7), and reports results in acceptable formats (I8). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because I4 and I6 are not satisfied.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD (bvFTD) group (n=33) and healthy controls (n=34). The paper reports voxel-based morphometry whole-brain group contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls (two-sample t-tests) with results reported in standard space (MNI) and peak coordinates (see Tables/Figures). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). Whole-brain voxelwise results are presented (cerebrum VBM with FWE-corrected thresholds), and additional seed coordinates and SUIT cerebellar analyses are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review objective and violates no exclusion criteria.

Excluded because the paper does not report a between-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast comparing a bvFTD (behavioral variant FTD) group to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space. The study uses VBM and reports voxelwise correlational analyses across a heterogeneous sample and co-atrophy checks, but does not present a standalone bvFTD vs control group-level whole-brain contrast. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3 (VBM used), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed FTD/bvFTD patients), I5 (sample sizes ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no reported bvFTD vs control between-group voxelwise contrast), I7 (no group-level whole-brain result clearly identified as coming solely from the bvFTD sample). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete.

Full text is complete. Study meets I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD; n=31), and I5 (bvFTD n>=6 and controls n=75). However, the neuroimaging analyses are covariate-based voxelwise regressions of BIS/BAS across the combined sample and co-atrophy checks; the paper does not present any between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD group directly to controls (in MNI/Talairach space) nor any bvFTD-specific whole-brain group-level voxelwise result. Therefore it fails I6 and I7 required by the review. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) appear to be met. Exclude on the basis of missing I6 and I7.

This empirical study meets all required inclusion criteria for the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis. It used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), included a clearly defined frontal-variant/behavioral variant FTD group (FTD-fv) (I4) with n=25 and healthy controls (n=14) (I5). The paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts and cluster coordinates in Montreal Neurological Institute space comparing FTD-fv to controls (I6), and provides whole-brain voxelwise results identified for the target sample group (I7). Coordinates and region descriptions are reported in text/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (no review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, no prohibited modalities, and sample exclusions appropriately applied). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is sufficiently complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This empirical study used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports voxelwise group contrasts and voxelwise covariate analyses with MNI coordinates comparing bvFTD patients to healthy controls. The bvFTD sample (n=24) and control sample (n=22) both exceed the minimum size. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (bvFTD vs Controls) are reported (tables/figures) and anatomical coordinates are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not a review, not ROI-only, no disallowed imaging modality). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

The full text reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=57) (I4). Sample sizes meet minimum requirements for patients and controls (bvFTD n=57; controls n=30) (I5). The paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts and group-level whole-brain results comparing bvFTD to controls, with anatomical/coordinate reporting in MNI space and detailed VBM results (I6, I7, I8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study used voxel-based morphometry), I4 (bvFTD patients included, n=18), I5 (bvFTD and control groups exceed n≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD group directly to controls in MNI/Talairach coordinates is reported in the provided full text—the VBM results are reported as brain–behavior correlations across the full cohort rather than a bvFTD vs. HC contrast), and I7 (no clearly identified group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result specifically reported as coming from the bvFTD group is provided in the text/tables as presented). Exclusion criteria met: none (no ROI-only restriction, not a review, no disallowed modality). Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the paper is excluded because it does not report the required between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast for the bvFTD group vs controls (I6/I7 not satisfied).

The study examines FTLD (frontotemporal lobar degeneration) but does not specify that patients were diagnosed with the behavioral variant (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease; thus inclusion criterion I4 is not met. Although the paper uses voxel-wise FDG‑PET and MRI analyses (I3 satisfied), appears to have adequate group sizes for analyses (I5 satisfied), and reports whole-brain results in maps/tables (I8 satisfied), it does not report any group-level, whole-brain contrast specifically comparing a clinically diagnosed bvFTD (or Pick’s) group to controls (I6 and I7 not met). No exclusion criteria from the review (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the bvFTD imaging meta-analysis. It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality, includes clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD (both sporadic bvFTD and C9ORF72 mutation carriers), and reports adequate sample sizes (sporadic bvFTD n=15; C9 n=8; Controls n=15). The paper provides whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (each patient group vs. controls) with results referenced to MNI space and detailed voxelwise analyses (permutation testing, cluster results, and anatomical labeling). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only analyses, prohibited imaging modalities, or comorbid samples) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

Although this study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3 satisfied), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=28) (I4 satisfied), and meets sample size requirements for patients and controls (I5 satisfied), it does not report any whole-brain, group-level between-group VBM contrasts that directly compare the bvFTD group to healthy controls in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The imaging results are voxelwise correlations across a mixed diagnostic sample (polisher/tarnisher subsamples and whole-sample correlations) rather than a bvFTD-versus-control group contrast; therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria from the provided list apply.

Decision: EXCLUDED.
(a) Exclusion IDs met: none.
(b) Inclusion IDs met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (bvFTD group n=11 ≥6), I7 (reports whole-brain voxel-wise TBM results for the bvFTD group), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/text).
(c) Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (imaging modality is tensor-based morphometry [TBM], not VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no comparison of bvFTD group to healthy controls; between-group contrasts are bvFTD vs early-onset AD, not controls).
Full text completeness: fulltext_incomplete=false. 
Conclusion: Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants, adequate sample size, and reports whole-brain voxel-wise TBM analyses, it does not meet modality requirements (I3) nor provide the required bvFTD vs healthy-control whole-brain contrasts (I6) required for inclusion in this meta-analysis, so it must be excluded.

This is an empirical study using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on T1-weighted MRI and reports group-level voxelwise contrasts with MNI coordinates. It includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=26) and healthy controls (n=18), both above the 6-participant minimum. The paper reports between-group whole-brain VBM results for bvFTD versus controls (thresholding and coordinates in MNI space) and separate contrasts versus SD, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only analyses, excluded imaging modalities, or prohibited patient comorbidities) are met based on the full text. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion provided. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not clearly provide a between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrast comparing a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (not pooled with other patient groups) to controls in stereotactic coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I5 (patient and control sample sizes meet the ≥6 threshold for the MRI subgroup: patients n=32, controls n=27). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the sample is described as FTLD with SOC/EXEC and APH subgroups but the paper does not explicitly label or report analyses for a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group), I6 (no clear between-group contrast reported that compares a bvFTD group to controls in MNI/Talairach space without pooling), I7 (no clearly identified whole-brain group-level voxelwise result specifically coming from a bvFTD/bvFTD-equivalent sample in the text/tables provided). Exclusion IDs met: none ([]). Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This paper is a study protocol (no original empirical results). Exclusion E8 applies: non-empirical paper without original data. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (protocol includes resting-state BOLD fMRI), I4 (recruits FTD syndromes using Rascovsky criteria, which target bvFTD), I5 (plans to recruit ≥16 participants per diagnostic group). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 and I7 — the manuscript contains no between-group, whole-brain voxelwise results (no coordinates/MNI/Talairach contrasts) comparing bvFTD to controls. Therefore it cannot contribute coordinate-based whole-brain data required by the review. Full text appears complete (protocol with methods) but lacks results. Exclusion applied: E8.

Excluded because the study reports only ROI/tract-based cortical thickness, DWI tract metrics, and seed/ROI functional connectivity rather than whole-brain voxelwise results with stereotactic coordinates. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (only ROI analyses/no whole-brain voxelwise results) and E9 (only reports seed-based FC, DTI/tract metrics, or cortical thickness methods). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3 (resting-state fMRI was acquired and used), I4 (bvFTD patients included, N=10), I5 (bvFTD and healthy control groups each ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no explicit between-group contrasts reported as stereotactic coordinates in MNI/Talairach space for bvFTD vs controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly reported from the bvFTD sample), and I8 (no coordinate tables/whole-brain voxelwise results in text/supplement evident). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain analyses and reports group-level voxelwise comparisons of behavioural-variant FTD groups (C9ORF72, MAPT, GRN, sporadic bvFTD) versus controls and direct between-group contrasts. Clinical samples consist of bvFTD patients (all genetic groups and sporadic bvFTD) and a control group. Each patient group exceeds the minimum sample size (C9ORF72 n=19, MAPT n=25, GRN n=12, sporadic bvFTD n=20) and controls n=40. Whole-brain voxelwise results are described (VBM with SPM5, family-wise error correction) and presented in figures/tables; thus group-level whole-brain evidence from the target bvFTD samples is available. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study meets all imaging and sample criteria for inclusion. It uses voxel-based morphometry (voxelwise GM density analyses) comparing 63 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (Rascovsky criteria) to 55 demographically-matched healthy controls (I3, I4, I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts (bvFTD vs. controls) using nonparametric permutation testing and FWE correction, with results presented as clusters and peak loci converted to Talairach (coordinates reported) (I6, I7, I8). Sample sizes exceed the minimum required. The full text includes methods, results, and figures/tables supporting whole-brain VBM findings. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, no disallowed modalities or comorbid-sample issues). Therefore the study should be included.

This study is an open-label FDG-PET investigation in a mixed FTD sample and does not provide a between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls in stereotactic space. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses FDG-PET), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants), I5 (bvFTD subgroup n=7 ≥6), I7 (reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results for the sample and for bvFTD subgroup), I8 (results reported with coordinates/MNI-Talairach). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no between-group contrast of bvFTD versus controls in MNI/Talairach space; only within-subject before-vs-after and subgroup SPM analyses without a healthy/control group). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Therefore the paper must be excluded for the purposes of this meta-analysis focused on between-group bvFTD vs control voxelwise contrasts.

The study uses VBM (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD subgroup (n=21) meeting the minimum patient group size (I4, I5). However, the paper does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast (in MNI/Talairach space) that compares bvFTD alone to healthy controls with whole-brain group-level voxelwise results clearly attributed to the bvFTD sample (I6 and I7 are not satisfied based on the provided full text). Although VBM analyses and comparisons to healthy controls are referenced (some results said to be in Supplementary material), no explicit coordinates or whole-brain bvFTD-vs-control voxelwise results for the bvFTD group are presented in the available full text. No exclusion criteria from the review (E5–E9) appear to apply. Therefore the study cannot be included for this meta-analysis because it fails to meet the required between-group, whole-brain reporting requirements (I6 and I7).

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it employs voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and FDG-PET (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients using Rascovsky criteria (I4), has ≥6 patients and controls (15 each) (I5), reports voxelwise between-group SPM analyses normalized to standard space allowing BV-FTD vs control contrasts (I6), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (I7/I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; therefore fulltext is complete.

This study reports whole-brain, voxelwise FDG-PET (SPM) analyses with coordinates (MNI converted to Talairach) comparing clinically diagnosed FTD groups to controls. The sample meets size requirements (FTD n=29; FTD/MND n=8; controls n=11). All patients fulfilled consensus clinical diagnostic criteria for FTD (Neary et al.); the paper reports that most patients presented behavioral symptoms, consistent with behavioral-variant FTD. The paper provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results and coordinates (including supplementary table). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not a non-empirical paper, and not an irrelevant modality). Full text appears complete (includes introduction/background, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical VBM study of bvFTD using whole-brain voxelwise analyses. The paper uses voxel-based morphometry on T1-weighted MRI (preprocessed in CAT12/SPM12, normalized to MNI space), reports group-level VBM contrasts comparing 82 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients to 80 healthy controls with voxelwise results (FDR/FWE thresholds, cluster tables/figures referenced). Disease staging is specified and bvFTD is not pooled with other patient groups. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (reviews, ROI-only, non-empirical, seed-only FC/DTI/cortical thickness, or comorbid-sample issues) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and is eligible for inclusion.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants) and I5 (sample sizes: bvFTD n=57 and controls n=172 exceed minimum). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 — imaging modality is structural T1 volumetry/parcellation and SuStaIn regional volumetric analysis, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET; I6 and I7 — the paper reports region/parcel/cluster-level volumetric comparisons and SuStaIn-derived maps, not group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (only ROI/parcel-based analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is a multimodal, empirical imaging study including a bvFTD group (N=10) and healthy controls (N=113). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (used T1 morphometry and resting-state fMRI), I4 (included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (bvFTD and control groups ≥6 subjects). However, the paper reports ROI-based cerebellar volumetrics, tractography, and ROI-to-ROI functional connectivity and presents groupwise statistics/tables; it does not present any clearly identified whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) with coordinates for bvFTD vs controls. Therefore it fails I6 and I7 (and I8 is not satisfied because no whole-brain voxelwise coordinates/figures are provided). This meets exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI/tract-based analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

This study examines MAPT mutation carriers stratified as asymptomatic, prodromal, and symptomatic, not a cohort of clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) patients compared directly to controls. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (resting-state fMRI was used) and I5 (sample sizes exceed 6 for patient and control groups). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 — participants are genetic MAPT mutation carriers, not explicitly a clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick's disease group; I6 — the paper does not report between-group voxelwise contrasts in standard stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) comparing a bvFTD group to controls; I7 — it does not present whole-brain voxelwise results specifically for a clinically defined bvFTD group (functional results are parcel/graph-based and structural results are surface-based FreeSurfer vertex analyses without MNI/Talairach coordinate tables tied to a bvFTD diagnostic group). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were triggered. Therefore the paper does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis and is excluded.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry and reports whole-brain voxelwise W-score/atrophy maps comparing bvFTD patients to controls, includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=117) and >6 controls, and presents group-level whole-brain results/figures. However, the provided full text does not present stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) or explicit coordinate tables for between-group contrasts required by criterion I6. Therefore I apply inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I7, and I8, but I6 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Because the meta-analysis requires reported coordinates for voxelwise between-group contrasts, this paper must be excluded.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality inclusion criterion (I3). This paper uses 18F-flortaucipir tau-PET and MR-based FreeSurfer volumetry rather than Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM), fMRI (resting or task), or FDG-PET required by I3. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (sample sizes: 20 bvFTD, 20 controls), I6 (reports between-group voxelwise comparisons after spatial normalization), and I7 (reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level results for bvFTD vs controls). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (required imaging modality). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical study that used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on 3T structural MRI and reports whole-brain voxelwise group contrasts. The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (N=20 overall; N=17 in MRI analyses) and healthy controls (N=39 overall; N=28 in MRI analyses), exceeding the minimum group sizes. The paper reports VBM atrophy comparisons of bvFTD versus healthy controls and voxelwise correlations of prosocial giving with gray matter volume, including whole-brain follow-up analyses with reported cluster coordinates (e.g., cerebellum coordinates) and clear anatomical localization. The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; not seed-FC/DTI/cortical thickness only). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an exclusion. The study is an MRI volumetry study using manual tracing of the putamen on T1-weighted structural scans (ROI volumetric analysis), not Voxel-Based Morphometry, fMRI, or FDG‑PET, so it fails inclusion criterion I3. It does not report any stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) coordinate-based between-group contrasts nor any whole-brain voxelwise group-level results, failing I6 and I7. The study does include clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia (FTD) patients (likely the behavioral/FTD subgroup) and meets sample-size criterion (FTD n=12; controls n=25), so I4 and I5 are satisfied. Because it reports only region-of-interest volumetric analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results, exclusion criterion E6 applies. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I6, I7. Exclusion criteria met: E6.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key imaging and result reporting criteria required by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (bvFTD patients included as a reference group, n=9) and I5 (patient group and control group sizes ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modalities used are ASL, DTI, and volumetric GM measures—not VBM, task or resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls), and I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results provided for the target sample). No exclusion criteria from the provided list are directly met. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it reports only lobar/ROI volumetry and group comparisons on region volumes rather than whole-brain, voxelwise stereotactic results. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses automated voxel-based volumetry based on SPM5, analogous to VBM), I4 (includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTLD subgroup), I5 (bvFTLD N=6 and controls N=30). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrast reported in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTLD to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified from the target sample), I8 (not applicable as no voxelwise tables/coordinates provided). Exclusion criterion met: E6 (reports only ROI/lobar analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study does not provide the required stereotactic, whole-brain voxelwise coordinates/results and is excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not study clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s disease patients (it studies asymptomatic MAPT mutation carriers, some of whom later developed MCI or bvFTD features), and it does not use one of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). Although the paper reports whole-brain voxelwise tensor-based morphometry (TBM) results comparing MAPT carriers (n=14) to noncarriers (n=13), it does not present between-group contrasts of a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group versus controls in standard stereotactic space, so key inclusion criteria are not met.

This study is excluded because, although it uses FDG-PET and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=6), it does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing the bvFTD group to controls. Analyses were performed using region-of-interest (ROI) measures and visual inspection; no coordinates or voxelwise group-level results are provided, and there is no control group comparison presented for bvFTD. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET used), I4 (bvFTD patients included), I5 (bvFTD group size = 6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrast vs controls), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level result). Exclusion criterion met: E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This study should be excluded because it reports ROI-based diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) results rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET whole-brain voxelwise analyses required by the review. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (study uses only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and E9 (study reports DTI rather than allowed modalities). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample present) and I5 (patient and control group sizes ≥6: 8 bvFTD, 12 controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is DTI, not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach space), and I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper does not satisfy the modality and whole-brain voxelwise requirements and must be excluded.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) cohort (n=10) and a control group (n=10). The paper performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise VBM contrasts comparing each disease cohort (including bvFTD) to controls (results reported in template/MNI space or in cohort-specific template space) and reports VBM outputs and thresholded maps. The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled with other patient groups). The report includes whole-brain, voxelwise results (figures and described contrasts). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria relevant to the review (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study is excluded because it does not report any between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD patients to healthy controls in stereotactic space (Criterion I6 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET imaging), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (sample size N=31 ≥6), I7 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results within the bvFTD sample), and I8 (coordinates/MNI space reported). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore exclusion is based on failure to provide a between-group bvFTD vs control whole-brain contrast (I6).

This study meets several inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=30) (I4), and has adequate sample sizes for patients and controls (I5). The paper reports voxelwise structural results with coordinates/cluster locations (e.g., MNI-like coordinates) from group-level analyses (I7). However, it does not report a direct between-group voxelwise contrast of bvFTD versus healthy controls (i.e., a between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach space where bvFTD is contrasted against controls) or such a result is not clearly presented; the neuroimaging results focus on voxelwise correlations of atrophy with physiological/behavioral measures and lateralization indices rather than a straightforward bvFTD>control or bvFTD<control contrast. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 is not met. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Exclusion criteria: none applied.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis: (1) Imaging modality: voxel-based morphometry (VBM) was used (I3). (2) Sample: includes a clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD (bvFTD) group (n=10) (I4). (3) Sample sizes: bvFTD group (n=10) and control group (n=14) both ≥6 (I5). (4) Between-group contrasts: VBM t-tests comparing bvFTD to controls were reported (I6). (5) Whole-brain evidence: group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results are reported for the bvFTD group (I7). (6) Results reported in standard space: MNI coordinates and tables/figures are provided (I8). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, no prohibited modalities). Full text appears complete (methods, results, VBM tables/figures, discussion). Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical FDG-PET SPM study of clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (n=17), exceeding the minimum sample size. The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM analyses (single-subject comparisons to a normative FDG-PET database and group-level SPM results overlaid on an MNI template) and presents group-level voxelwise findings linking hypometabolism to socio-emotional deficits. These analyses constitute between-group contrasts against a normative control database and provide whole-brain results in stereotactic space, satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review paper, ROI-only, seed-based FC/DTI/cortical-thickness only, or comorbid psychiatric/other dementia confounds) are met. Full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and satisfies the reporting allowance I8.

Although the study uses VBM and resting-state fMRI and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases with adequate sample sizes, the analyses combine bvFTD and avPPA into a single FTD-GRN+ group and do not report any voxelwise between-group contrasts specifically comparing a bvFTD-only group to controls.
