Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (no bvFTD-specific whole-brain contrasts reported). Full text appears complete.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=21) and healthy controls (n=46), and reports whole-brain VBM results in tables/figures. However, it does not report a voxelwise between-group contrast comparing the bvFTD group directly to controls in MNI or Talairach space. The imaging analyses are primarily correlational across a mixed diagnostic sample (and analyses of ‘overestimators’/‘underestimators’), and although diagnostic group membership was used as a covariate in some analyses, no clear bvFTD vs. control whole-brain group-level contrast is presented. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7. Full text appears complete.

Although this study meets multiple inclusion requirements (it uses FDG-PET imaging [I3], includes a clinically-diagnosed bvFTD sample [37 patients, I4], has adequate patient sample size [I5], and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise regression analyses within the bvFTD sample [I7]), it does NOT report a between-group contrast comparing the bvFTD group to healthy controls in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The paper uses patient vs. normative-control database comparisons to define individual hypometabolism and performs regression analyses within the patient group (occupation vs. metabolism), but no group-level bvFTD vs. control voxelwise contrast in stereotactic coordinates is provided. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and includes 20 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, meeting I3, I4 and the sample-size requirement I5. However, it does not report any between-group contrasts comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space (fails I6). Analyses were performed within a frontal mask rather than reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (fails I7). Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I6 and I7 are not satisfied, the study should be excluded from this meta-analysis.

The full text reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (SPM99) relating bvFTD patients to healthy controls, including two-sample t-tests and regression analyses linking IRI empathy scores to gray-matter atrophy. Imaging modality is VBM (I3). The sample includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (N=12) (I4) and imaging controls (N=12), satisfying sample size requirements (I5). The paper reports between-group VBM contrasts of bvFTD versus controls and voxelwise results with cluster thresholds and a results table/figure (Table 2, Figure 1) in standardized coordinates via SPM (I6, I7). Results are presented in tables/figures described in the text (I8). No exclusion criteria apply; the study is empirical, not a review, includes whole-brain VBM results (not ROI-only), and excludes other dementia causes per methods. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). The study uses FDG-PET (I3), includes clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD patients within the sample (I4), has sufficient sample sizes (bvFTD n=21; controls n>=6) (I5), and reports voxelwise whole-brain results/tables for the FTLD group (I8). However, it does NOT present a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrast that isolates a bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) group compared directly to healthy controls without pooling with other FTLD subtypes. Therefore it fails I6 (no bvFTD-vs-control between-group contrast) and I7 (no clearly identified whole-brain voxelwise result coming specifically from a bvFTD target group). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Because the meta-analysis requires bvFTD-specific, group-level whole-brain contrasts reported in stereotactic space, this paper must be excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (fails I3) and reports only ROI-based volumetric and shape analyses of the caudate and putamen without whole-brain voxelwise results in MNI/Talairach space (fails I6 and I7). Exclusion criterion E6 applies (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample) and I5 (≥6 patients and ≥6 controls). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study is excluded because it does not meet key imaging and whole-brain voxelwise reporting criteria required by the review. Exclusion IDs met: E6 (the study reports only ROI-based analyses with no whole-brain/voxelwise results). Inclusion IDs met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients) and I5 (patient and control group sizes meet the >=6 requirement: bvFTD n=11, controls n=20). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (study uses structural ROI analyses and ASL perfusion, not VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrast results reported in standard stereotactic space with MNI/Talairach coordinates for bvFTD vs controls), and I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results). Full text appears complete; exclusion is based on methodological and reporting criteria.

The study uses VBM (I3) and has adequate group sizes (37 FTD patients, controls) meeting I5. However, the patient sample is a heterogeneous FTD group (only a small subset explicitly described as behavioural-variant FTD) and the analyses and reported results treat FTD as a pooled group rather than reporting results for a clinically-diagnosed bvFTD subgroup separately. The paper does not present a clear group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrast in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) for a bvFTD-only group; results are reported mainly as ROI-wise classification accuracies rather than voxel-coordinate tables or explicit whole-brain maps for bvFTD. Therefore it fails I4 (bvFTD sample not isolated) and I6/I7 (no bvFTD-specific whole-brain voxelwise, stereotactic-coordinate results). Exclusion criterion E6 applies because the reported results are effectively ROI-based without the required whole-brain voxelwise coordinates/maps for the target bvFTD group.

The study meets I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients: 16 bvFTD cases within 26 FTLD patients), and I5 (patient n=26; control n=21). However, it does NOT meet I6: the paper does not report any between-group voxelwise contrast in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing a bvFTD group to controls—the VBM analyses are within the combined FTLD cohort (and no MR images were acquired for controls). It also does NOT meet I7: there are whole-brain voxelwise results, but these are reported for the combined FTLD sample, not as a group-level, whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target group. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded because key inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not satisfied.

This study used VBM (I3), included adequate group sizes (I5), and reports whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates (I7,I8). However, the sample comprises heterogeneous FTD phenotypes (GRN+ and GRN- FTD) rather than a clearly defined bvFTD (behavioural-variant FTD) group, and no between-group contrast is reported that compares a bvFTD-only group to controls. Therefore it does not meet I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick's disease) nor I6 (between-group contrast of bvFTD vs controls). Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study does not meet the imaging and whole-brain analysis requirements. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (the study reports only linear/region-based measures—Bifrontal Index—without any whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed Frontotemporal Dementia patients using Neary et al. criteria), I5 (patient group size n=23, ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (did not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET; used linear MRI measurements), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD to controls; no control voxelwise comparison reported), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results presented). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an original empirical multicenter study including resting-state fMRI and voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3). It enrolled 52 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and 60 healthy controls (I4, I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise VBM analyses normalized to MNI space with two-sample t-tests and FWE-corrected results, and presents group-level between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls (I6, I7). Whole-brain results are reported in figures and Supporting Information tables (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: it is not a review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, includes no psychiatric comorbidity pooling, is empirical with original data, and does not rely solely on seed FC/DTI/cortical thickness (E5–E9 not applicable). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is excluded because it does not use an eligible imaging modality per inclusion criterion I3: it uses SPECT perfusion imaging rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET. Included criteria met: I4 (the sample includes clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD/fvFTD patients) and I5 (patient group n=48 and control group n=15, both ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality not eligible), I6 (the paper does not clearly report a between-group whole-brain contrast in MNI/Talairach space specifically comparing a bvFTD-only group to controls in the main reported results), and I7 (it is not clear that at least one whole-brain voxelwise group-level result is reported specifically for the bvFTD target group). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets the review objectives and inclusion criteria. It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to derive W-score atrophy maps in standard MNI space (I3). The sample includes neuropathologically confirmed Pick's disease patients (n=27), which satisfies inclusion for Pick's disease participants (I4) and exceeds the minimum group size (I5). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise atrophy maps for each FTLD subtype (including Pick's disease) are reported and available in MNI space (NeuroVault), meeting the requirement for a whole-brain group-level result from the target sample (I6, I7). Whole-brain results are presented in figures and made available as maps, which is acceptable per the criteria (I8). No exclusion criteria were met. Full text appears complete.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E9 — the study uses cortical thickness and visual atrophy scales (VAS) and MRPI rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET; methods include cortical thickness (surface-based) analyses which are specifically excluded. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I4 — sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants; I5 — sample sizes exceed minimum (bvFTD groups >6 participants; controls n=225). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I3 — imaging modality requirement (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) is not satisfied; I6 and I7 — the paper does not report between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space from VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET (no eligible coordinate-based whole-brain results in the required modalities). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This FDG-PET study does not meet key inclusion criteria for the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses FDG-PET), I5 (patient group n=14 and control group n=33, both ≥6). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (participants are pathologically confirmed FTLD and AD but not specified as clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD or Pick's disease), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach space for a bvFTD group), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results reported). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (analysis is region-based/visual ratings rather than whole-brain voxelwise results / coordinates). Full text appears complete. Because it lacks a clearly defined bvFTD patient group and does not provide whole-brain voxelwise coordinate results, it must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain analyses (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), has adequate sample sizes (24 bvFTD patients, 179 controls; I5), and reports between-group voxelwise contrasts with MNI coordinates (I6). The paper presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (interaction and group contrasts) clearly in the text and supplementary material (I7,I8). No exclusion criteria are met: this is an empirical VBM study (not a review, ROI-only, DTI, cortical thickness-only, or seed-based FC study), and there is no indication of disqualifying comorbid samples. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and supplementary references). Therefore, include for the meta-analysis of bvFTD VBM studies.

This study uses FDG-PET and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (meets I3, I4) with sufficient sample size (15 bvFTD/fd+ cases; meets I5). However, it does not report any between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls, nor does it provide coordinate tables or group-level voxelwise results (fails I6 and I7). The imaging results are presented as qualitative reads and diagnostic accuracy (sensitivity/specificity), not as voxelwise group contrasts. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E6 (no whole-brain results / only non-coordinate qualitative imaging) and does not satisfy required inclusion criteria I6 and I7. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the bvFTD imaging meta-analysis. Imaging modality: voxel-based morphometry (VBM) was used (I3). Sample includes an autopsy-confirmed/biomarker-negative behavioural variant FTD (bvFTD) group (n=59) (I4) with matched healthy controls (n=61), satisfying sample size requirements (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxel-wise contrasts comparing bvFTD patients to controls (adjusted voxel-wise VBM contrasts, p-values, and coordinate tables referenced in Supplementary Table 1), providing results in standard stereotactic space (coordinates) (I6, I7). Whole-brain results are clearly described in text, figures, and supplementary materials (I8). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/supplement). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered.

This VBM study meets I3 (uses voxel-based morphometry), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within the FTLD cohort), and I5 (sample size: 37 FTLD patients, bvFTD subgroup >6). However it does NOT meet I6 or I7: the reported voxelwise contrasts compare musicophilic vs non-musicophilic FTLD subgroups (and include syndromic group as a covariate) rather than presenting any between-group contrast of bvFTD versus healthy controls (in MNI/Talairach space) where bvFTD is not pooled with other patient groups. Although whole-brain VBM analyses are reported, they are not clearly identified as originating from a bvFTD-vs-control comparison. No exclusion criteria from the provided list apply. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to provide the required bvFTD-to-control voxelwise whole-brain contrast (I6, I7 not met).

The study is excluded because it does not use an accepted imaging modality for this review (I3 not met) and it does not report whole-brain voxelwise results in a standard stereotactic space (I6/I7 not met). Instead, the paper reports region-of-interest cortical and subcortical volumetric correlations derived from Freesurfer parcellation (ROI-based structural volumetry), and no MNI/Talairach coordinates or voxelwise statistical maps are provided. This meets exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). The study does satisfy inclusion criteria I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, N=32) and I5 (patient group and control group sizes ≥6), and the full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a study protocol/methods paper (LEFFTDS) describing planned longitudinal data collection and MRI acquisition. It does not present original empirical neuroimaging results or any group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients to controls. While the protocol includes planned fMRI acquisition (I3 satisfied), it contains no reported clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group data, no between-group contrasts in MNI/Talairach space, and no whole-brain results (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8 not met). As a non-empirical methods-only paper without original data, it meets exclusion criterion E8.

This empirical study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain analyses (methods and MNI coordinates reported) to examine grey-matter correlates of psychosis in a clinically diagnosed bvFTD cohort (bvFTD and bvFTD-ALS). Sample sizes meet thresholds (56 patients, 23 controls). The paper reports voxelwise between-group contrasts and whole-brain, group-level results in MNI space (permutation-based GLM, FWE-corrected and uncorrected cluster results, with supplementary coordinate tables). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplementary tables/figures noted. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not solely other imaging modalities or non-empirical). Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clearly defined behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) subgroup (11 bvFTD participants) and healthy controls (15). Voxel-based morphometry was used and whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons (patient subgroups vs controls) and voxelwise correlations are reported and overlaid in MNI space; results (including cluster-level findings and figures/tables) are described in main text and supplementary materials. Sample sizes meet the ≥6 participant requirement for patient and control groups. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results attributable specifically to the bvFTD group (bvFTD vs controls) and provides coordinates/overlays in MNI space. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review only, ROI-only analyses, non-empirical, irrelevant imaging modality, disallowed patient comorbidities) are violated. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, imaging analyses) is present. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7,I8) and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis focused on bvFTD VBM studies.

This study should be excluded because it does not meet the imaging- and analysis-related inclusion criteria required by the review. Although it includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (N=36) satisfying I4 and meets the minimum patient sample size (I5), it does not use one of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) — imaging used was structural MRI/CT and PET/SPECT without indication of FDG-PET (I3 not met). Crucially, the paper presents no between-group voxelwise contrasts in a standardized stereotactic space comparing bvFTD to controls, and there is no healthy control group or whole-brain group-level voxelwise results (I6 and I7 not met; I8 therefore not applicable). No exclusion criteria are specifically triggered by the study content. Full text appears complete.

The study meets I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients: 16 bvFTD cases within 26 FTLD patients), and I5 (patient n=26; control n=21). However, it does NOT meet I6: the paper does not report any between-group voxelwise contrast in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing a bvFTD group to controls—the VBM analyses are within the combined FTLD cohort (and no MR images were acquired for controls). It also does NOT meet I7: there are whole-brain voxelwise results, but these are reported for the combined FTLD sample, not as a group-level, whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target group. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded because key inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not satisfied.

This full text reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) results comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD (behavioural variant FTD) mutation carriers to healthy controls. VBM was used (I3). The sample includes bvFTD patients (I4) with n=7 patients in the VBM analysis and n=19 controls (I5). The paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts and significant clusters and refers to stereotactic locations in supplementary Table 4 (i.e., MNI/Talairach coordinates) (I6). Results are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise VBM findings clearly identified as coming from the target bvFTD sample and reported in text/figures/supplement (I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, and discussion).

Although the study uses FDG-PET and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=13) with an adequate control group (n=9), the imaging results are reported for a pooled FTD spectrum group (n=33) rather than for the behavioral-variant FTD subgroup alone. The meta-analysis requires group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts derived specifically from the bvFTD (or Pick’s disease) group that are not pooled with other patient subtypes. This study therefore fails to meet inclusion criteria I6 and I7. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET imaging), I4 (bvFTD patients included in sample), I5 (patient and control group sizes ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no bvFTD-specific between-group contrast reported), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target group). No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the bvFTD-focused review. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses MRI-based morphometry/ VBM/TBM), I5 (FTD patient group size = 30, control group size ≥6), I7 (reports whole-brain, voxelwise statistical parametric maps comparing patient group to controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (does not specifically report clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD or Pick's disease — the paper refers generically to 'FTD' without specifying subtype), I6 (does not report between-group contrast coordinates in a standard stereotactic space such as MNI or Talairach; analyses are performed in a group-wise template space and SPM figures are described but stereotactic coordinates/tables in MNI/Talairach are not provided). Exclusion criteria met: none (no applicable exclusion IDs). Full text completeness: fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study used 18F-FDG PET and reports whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses, and includes a clear FTD subgroup (26 FTD patients) with adequate sample sizes (>6). However, the reported between-group contrasts compare incontinent versus continent patients within the FTLD/FTD sample (FTLD+UIC vs FTLD−UIC), not bvFTD versus healthy controls. Inclusion criterion I6 requires a between-group contrast comparing bvFTD (behavioral FTD) to controls where bvFTD is not pooled with other patient groups; that contrast is not present. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded because it does not meet I6.

The study includes FDG-PET imaging (I3), enrolled clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within the sample (I4), and has sufficient sample sizes (10 patients, 10 controls) to meet I5. However it does NOT meet key inclusion criteria: (a) bvFTD subjects are pooled with other FTD subtypes in group analyses so there is no between-group contrast that isolates a bvFTD-only group vs controls (I6 not met), and (b) the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) MNI/Talairach result for the bvFTD group (group results are ROI-based and single-subject voxelwise maps are provided) so I7 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered by the study. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing I6 and I7.

This is an empirical FDG-PET study of clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (N=82) with an HC group (N=82). It applies whole-brain, voxel-wise SPM analyses (SPM t-maps, voxel-level and cluster-level FWE-corrected results) comparing bvFTD to controls and reports subgroup (frontal vs temporo-limbic) comparisons and resting-state network voxel-wise results. The imaging modality, sample, sample sizes, and reporting of group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts in stereotactic (SPM) space satisfy the review criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, includes whole-brain results, not limited to ROI-only or disallowed modalities, and sample does not include other dementia pooled with bvFTD). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this study uses VBM (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (13/16 likely bvFTD) with adequate sample sizes (patients n=16, controls n=9) satisfying I4 and I5, it does not report a between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrast comparing a bvFTD-only group to controls. The reported whole-brain VBM results are for the FTLD group as a whole and for within-FTLD behavioural covariates; no separate bvFTD vs control voxelwise results are presented. Therefore it fails I6 (no bvFTD-only between-group contrast) and I7 (no whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from the target bvFTD sample). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete.

While the study meets several inclusion criteria (I3: uses VBM; I4: includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=24); I5: patient group size >=6), it does NOT meet key criteria required for inclusion. The paper does not report any between-group contrasts comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space (I6 not met). It also does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) results that are specific to the bvFTD sample alone (I7 not met); the reported VBM analyses are regression/voxelwise correlations across a mixed patient cohort and the authors state analyses by individual patient groups produced no significant results. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete (contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to provide bvFTD-specific between-group whole-brain voxelwise results.

Although the study uses whole-brain VBM (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=12) and controls (n=21) meeting the sample size requirement (I4, I5), it does not report a between-group, voxelwise contrast in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) that directly compares bvFTD versus controls as an independent group-level result. The VBM results are reported as correlations of conjunction-search accuracy with gray matter across subjects and subsequent extracted-voxel ANOVAs comparing diagnostic groups, not as a primary whole-brain bvFTD>control or bvFTD<control contrast in stereotactic coordinates. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered by the manuscript. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Study uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes a sufficient number of FTD patients overall (I5). However, it does not specify that patients have behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease (I4 not met). The paper reports multivariate classification and discriminative images but does not provide a between-group voxelwise contrast in MNI/Talairach space specifically comparing a bvFTD group to controls (I6 and I7 not met). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for this review and is excluded.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD patients (I4); has sufficient sample sizes (11 bvFTD patients, 11 matched controls) meeting the minimum of 6 per group (I5); reports between-group voxelwise analyses comparing bvFTD to controls using voxel-wise two-sample t-tests (I6); provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (VBM) clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group (I7); and the whole-brain results are presented in figures/text (acceptable per I8). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not a review, not ROI-only, not an excluded imaging modality). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The study uses VBM and reports whole-brain voxelwise results with adequate sample sizes, but the sample is pathologically-defined FTLD-T and FTLD-U (and clinical diagnoses described broadly as frontotemporal dementia, with some PNFA/SD), not explicitly or exclusively clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease. Inclusion criterion I4 (must include clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease) is not met, and I6 (between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to controls) is not met because contrasts are FTLD-T vs controls and FTLD-U vs controls rather than a bvFTD-only group. Therefore the study does not address the target patient group for the meta-analysis and must be excluded.

Excluded because the study does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain/coordinate reporting inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants included) and I5 (patient group sizes: bvFTD n=14, AD n=19). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (study did not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG‑PET as the primary imaging modality for reported results—main analyses used FreeSurfer volumetry and DTI), I6 (no between-group results reported in MNI/Talairach coordinates), and I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported). Exclusion criteria applicable: E9 (study reports DTI and cortical/volumetric measures rather than VBM/fMRI/FDG‑PET) and E6 (analyses are ROI-based with no whole-brain voxelwise coordinate results). Full text appears complete.

Full text reports VBM (voxel-based morphometry) analyses alongside DTI, includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=29) and healthy controls (n=37), and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts and disease maps (bvFTD vs controls) using standard stereotactic analysis and permutation testing. Whole-brain VBM results are presented and summarized (with clusters/peaks referenced in figures/tables/supplementary material). The full article contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, so the full text appears complete and satisfies all required inclusion criteria without triggering any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, full-text study that uses voxel-based morphometry and task-free (resting‑state) functional MRI (I3). The sample comprises clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (meets Neary and FTDC criteria) including C9orf72+ and C9orf72− groups (I4). Patient group sizes (14 and 14; total n=28) and control groups (HC1 n=42 for VBM; HC2 n=14 for fMRI) exceed the minimum of 6 participants (I5).
